तस्यान्ते कुरुते सर्गं यथेदं कथितं तव ॥ 111
1.2.m: Such is a day of that great-souled Viriñci; / at its end he brings about creation, just as has been related to you.

1.2.s:
krīḍannivaitatkurute parameṣṭhī narādhipa .
catuṣpātsakalo dharmaḥ satyaṃ caiva kṛte yuge . . 112
1.2.d:
क्रीडन्निवैतत्कुरुते परमेष्ठी नराधिप ।
चतुष्पात्सकलो धर्मः सत्यं चैव कृते युगे ॥ 112
1.2.m: As if in sport Parameṣṭhin does this, O king. / In the Kṛta Yuga dharma stands complete on four feet, and truth alone [prevails].

1.2.s:
nādharmeṇāgamaḥ kaścinmanuṣyāṇāṃ pravartate .
itareṣvāgamāstāta dharmaśca kurunandana . . 113
1.2.d:
नाधर्मेणागमः कश्चिन्मनुष्याणां प्रवर्तते ।
इतरेष्वागमास्तात धर्मश्च कुरुनन्दन ॥ 113
1.2.m: No acquisition comes to men through adharma. / In the other [yugas], my dear, acquisitions and dharma, O joy of the Kurus,

1.2.s:
yādṛśāḥ parihīyante yathāha bhagavānmanuḥ 1 .
cauryāccāpyanṛtādrājanmāyābhiramitadyute . . 114
1.2.d:
यादृशाः परिहीयन्ते यथाह भगवान्मनुः 1 ।
चौर्याच्चाप्यनृताद्राजन्मायाभिरमितद्युते ॥ 114
1.2.m: dwindle proportionally, just as the venerable Manu stated. / Through theft, falsehood, and deceptions, O king of boundless splendor,

1.2.s:
pādena hīyate dharmastretādiṣu yugeṣu vai .
arogāḥ sarvasiddhārthāścaturvarṣaśatāyuṣaḥ . . 115
1.2.d:
पादेन हीयते धर्मस्त्रेतादिषु युगेषु वै ।
अरोगाः सर्वसिद्धार्थाश्चतुर्वर्षशतायुषः ॥ 115
1.2.m: dharma diminishes foot by foot in the Tretā and subsequent yugas. / [In the Kṛta Yuga men are] free from disease, all their aims accomplished, living four hundred years;

1.2.s:
kṛtatretādiṣu tveṣāṃ vayo hrasati pādaśaḥ .
vedoktamāyurāśīśca martyānāṃ kurunandana . . 116
1.2.d:
कृतत्रेतादिषु त्वेषां वयो ह्रसति पादशः ।
वेदोक्तमायुराशीश्च मर्त्यानां कुरुनन्दन ॥ 116
1.2.m: in the Tretā and the rest their lifespan decreases quarter by quarter, / as do the lifespan and blessings ordained by the Veda for mortals, O joy of the Kurus.

1.2.s:
karmaṇāṃ tu phalaṃ tāta phalatyanuyugaṃ sadā .
prabhāvaśca tathā loke phalatyeva śarīriṇām . . 117
1.2.d:
कर्मणां तु फलं तात फलत्यनुयुगं सदा ।
प्रभावश्च तथा लोके फलत्येव शरीरिणाम् ॥ 117
1.2.m: The fruit of actions always bears fruit according to the yuga, my dear, / and likewise the power of embodied beings bears fruit in the world.

1.2.s:
anye kṛtayuge dharmāstretāyāṃ dvāpare pare .
anye kaliyuge nṛṇāṃ yugadharmānurūpataḥ . . 118
1.2.d:
अन्ये कृतयुगे धर्मास्त्रेतायां द्वापरे परे ।
अन्ये कलियुगे नृणां युगधर्मानुरूपतः ॥ 118
1.2.m: One set of dharmas belongs to the Kṛta Yuga, others to the Tretā and Dvāpara, / and others to the Kali Yuga, in accordance with the dharma of each yuga.

1.2.s:
tapaḥ paraṃ kṛtayuge tretāyāṃ jñānamucyate .
dvāpare yajñamityāhurdānamekaṃ kalau yuge . . 119
1.2.d:
तपः परं कृतयुगे त्रेतायां ज्ञानमुच्यते ।
द्वापरे यज्ञमित्याहुर्दानमेकं कलौ युगे ॥ 119
1.2.m: Austerity is highest in the Kṛta Yuga, knowledge is proclaimed in the Tretā, / sacrifice in the Dvāpara, they say, and giving alone in the Kali Yuga.

1.2.s:
sarvasya rājansargasya guptyarthaṃ ca mahādyute .
mukhabāhūrupādānāṃ pṛthakkarmāṇyakalpayat . . 1.2.120
1.2.d:
सर्वस्य राजन्सर्गस्य गुप्त्यर्थं च महाद्युते ।
मुखबाहूरुपादानां पृथक्कर्माण्यकल्पयत् ॥ 1.2.120
1.2.m: And for the protection of all creation, O king of great splendor, / he assigned distinct duties from his mouth, arms, thighs, and feet.

1.2.s:
adhyāpanamadhyayanaṃ yajanaṃ yājanaṃ tathā .
dānaṃ pratigrahaṃ caiva brāhmaṇānāmakalpayat . . 121
1.2.d:
अध्यापनमध्ययनं यजनं याजनं तथा ।
दानं प्रतिग्रहं चैव ब्राह्मणानामकल्पयत् ॥ 121
1.2.m: Teaching, studying, sacrificing, conducting sacrifices for others, / giving, and receiving gifts he assigned to brāhmaṇas.

1.2.s:
prajānāṃ pālanaṃ rājandānamadhyayanaṃ tathā .
viṣayeṣu prasaktiṃ ca tathejyāṃ kṣatriyasya tu . . 122
1.2.d:
प्रजानां पालनं राजन्दानमध्ययनं तथा ।
विषयेषु प्रसक्तिं च तथेज्यां क्षत्रियस्य तु ॥ 122
1.2.m: Protecting the subjects, O king, giving, studying, / non-attachment to sense objects, and sacrifice for the kṣatriya;

1.2.s:
paśūnāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ dānamijyādhyayanameva ca .
vaṇikpathaṃ 1 kusīdaṃ ca vaiśyasya kṛṣireva ca . . 123
1.2.d:
पशूनां रक्षणं दानमिज्याध्ययनमेव च ।
वणिक्पथं 1 कुसीदं च वैश्यस्य कृषिरेव च ॥ 123
1.2.m: tending cattle, giving, sacrifice, studying, / trade, money-lending, and agriculture for the vaiśya.

1.2.s:
ekameva tu śūdrasya karma loke prakīrtitam .
eteṣāmeva varṇānāṃ śuśrūṣāmanupūrvaśaḥ . . 124
1.2.d:
एकमेव तु शूद्रस्य कर्म लोके प्रकीर्तितम् ।
एतेषामेव वर्णानां शुश्रूषामनुपूर्वशः ॥ 124
1.2.m: Only one duty was declared in the world for the śūdra: / service to these other varnas in order.

1.2.s:
puruṣasya sadā śreṣṭhaṃ nābherūrdhvaṃ nṛpottama .
tasmādapi śucitaraṃ mukhaṃ tāta svayambhuvaḥ . . 125
1.2.d:
पुरुषस्य सदा श्रेष्ठं नाभेरूर्ध्वं नृपोत्तम ।
तस्मादपि शुचितरं मुखं तात स्वयम्भुवः ॥ 125
1.2.m: The part above the navel is ever purest in a man, O best of kings; / purer even than that, my dear, is the mouth of the Self-born.

1.2.s:
tasmānmukhāddvijo jāta itīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ .
sarvasyaivāsya dharmasya dharmato brāhmaṇaḥ prabhuḥ . . 126
1.2.d:
तस्मान्मुखाद्द्विजो जात इतीयं वैदिकी श्रुतिः ।
सर्वस्यैवास्य धर्मस्य धर्मतो ब्राह्मणः प्रभुः ॥ 126
1.2.m: From that mouth the twice-born was born—such is the Vedic revelation; / by righteousness the brāhmaṇa is the master of all this dharma.

1.2.s:
sa sṛṣṭo brahmaṇā pūrvaṃ tapastaptvā kurūdvaha .
havyānāmiva kavyānāṃ sarvasyāpi ca guptaye . . 127
1.2.d:
स सृष्टो ब्रह्मणा पूर्वं तपस्तप्त्वा कुरूद्वह ।
हव्यानामिव कव्यानां सर्वस्यापि च गुप्तये ॥ 127
1.2.m: He was created of old by Brahmā, having performed tapas, O bearer of the Kuru line, / for the protection of oblations to gods and ancestors and of all else.

1.2.s:
aśnanti ca mukhenāsya havyāni tridivaukasaḥ .
kavyāni caiva pitaraḥ kimbhūtamadhikaṃ tataḥ . . 128
1.2.d:
अश्नन्ति च मुखेनास्य हव्यानि त्रिदिवौकसः ।
कव्यानि चैव पितरः किम्भूतमधिकं ततः ॥ 128
1.2.m: Through his mouth the heaven-dwellers eat the oblations to gods, / and the ancestors the oblations to ancestors; what being is superior to him?

1.2.s:
bhūtānāṃ prāṇinaḥ śreṣṭhāḥ prāṇināṃ buddhijīvinaḥ .
buddhimatsu narāḥ śreṣṭhā nareṣu brāhmaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ . . 129
1.2.d:
भूतानां प्राणिनः श्रेष्ठाः प्राणिनां बुद्धिजीविनः ।
बुद्धिमत्सु नराः श्रेष्ठा नरेषु ब्राह्मणाः स्मृताः ॥ 129
1.2.m: Among beings, living creatures are best; among living creatures, those living by intellect; / among the intelligent, men are best; among men, brāhmaṇas are traditionally considered [highest].

1.2.s:
brāhmaṇeṣu ca vidvāṃso vidvatsu kṛtabuddhayaḥ .
kṛtabuddhiṣu kartāraḥ kartṛṣu brahmavedinaḥ . . 1.2.130
1.2.d:
ब्राह्मणेषु च विद्वांसो विद्वत्सु कृतबुद्धयः ।
कृतबुद्धिषु कर्तारः कर्तृषु ब्रह्मवेदिनः ॥ 1.2.130
1.2.m: Among brāhmaṇas, the learned; among the learned, those of firm resolve; / among those of firm resolve, the actors; among the actors, knowers of Brahman.

1.2.s:
janma viprasya rājendra dhamārthamiha kathyate .
utpannaḥ sarvasiddhayarthaṃ4 yāti brahmasado nṛpa . . 131
1.2.d:
जन्म विप्रस्य राजेन्द्र धमार्थमिह कथ्यते ।
उत्पन्नः सर्वसिद्धयर्थं4 याति ब्रह्मसदो नृप ॥ 131
1.2.m: The birth of a vipra is said to be for the sake of dharma in this world, O king of kings; / born for the fulfillment of all aims, he attains the abode of Brahman, O king.

1.2.s:
sa cāpi jāyamānastu pṛthivyāmiha jāyate .
bhūtānāṃ prabhavāyaiva dharmakośasya guptaye . . 132
1.2.d:
स चापि जायमानस्तु पृथिव्यामिह जायते ।
भूतानां प्रभवायैव धर्मकोशस्य गुप्तये ॥ 132
1.2.m: And he, being born, is born here upon the earth / for the very origination of beings, for the safeguarding of the treasure-house of dharma.

1.2.s:
sarvaṃ hi brāhmaṇasyedaṃ yatkiñcitpṛthivīgatam .
janmanā cottamenedaṃ sarvaṃ vai brāhmaṇo'rhati . . 133
1.2.d:
सर्वं हि ब्राह्मणस्येदं यत्किञ्चित्पृथिवीगतम् ।
जन्मना चोत्तमेनेदं सर्वं वै ब्राह्मणोऽर्हति ॥ 133
1.2.m: All whatever exists on earth belongs to the brāhmaṇa; / by his pre-eminent birth the brāhmaṇa is entitled to it all.

1.2.s:
svakīyaṃ brāhmaṇo bhuṅkte vidadhāti ca suvrata .
karuṇāṃ kurvatastasya bhuñjantī hetare janāḥ . . 134
1.2.d:
स्वकीयं ब्राह्मणो भुङ्क्ते विदधाति च सुव्रत ।
करुणां कुर्वतस्तस्य भुञ्जन्ती हेतरे जनाः ॥ 134
1.2.m: The brāhmaṇa eats and wears what is his own, O one of good vows; / it is through his benevolence that other men eat here.

1.2.s:
trayāṇāmiha varṇānāṃ bhāvābhāvāya vai dvijaḥ .
bhavedrājanna sandehastuṣṭo bhāvāya vai dvijaḥ . . 135
1.2.d:
त्रयाणामिह वर्णानां भावाभावाय वै द्विजः ।
भवेद्राजन्न सन्देहस्तुष्टो भावाय वै द्विजः ॥ 135
1.2.m: The twice-born exists for the being or non-being of the three varnas; / satisfied, the twice-born brings about existence—there is no doubt, O king.

1.2.s:
abhāvāya bhavetkruddhastasmātpūjyatamo hi saḥ .
brāhmaṇe sati nānyasya prabhutvaṃ vidyate nṛpa . .. 136
1.2.d:
अभावाय भवेत्क्रुद्धस्तस्मात्पूज्यतमो हि सः ।
ब्राह्मणे सति नान्यस्य प्रभुत्वं विद्यते नृप ॥। 136
1.2.m: Enraged, he would bring about non-being; therefore he is most worthy of honor. / When the brāhmaṇa exists, no other holds lordship, O king.

1.2.s:
kāmātkarotyasau karma kāmagaśca nṛpottama .
tasmādvṛndārakapurī tasmādapi mahaḥ punaḥ . . 137
1.2.d:
कामात्करोत्यसौ कर्म कामगश्च नृपोत्तम ।
तस्माद्वृन्दारकपुरी तस्मादपि महः पुनः ॥ 137
1.2.m: At will he performs actions, going wherever he wishes, O best of kings; / thence to the city of the gods, and from there to Mahas again,

1.2.s:
maharlokājjanolokaṃ brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati .
brahmatvaṃ ca mahābāho yāti vipro na saṃśayaḥ . . 138
1.2.d:
महर्लोकाज्जनोलोकं ब्रह्मलोकं च गच्छति ।
ब्रह्मत्वं च महाबाहो याति विप्रो न संशयः ॥ 138
1.2.m: from Maharloka he goes to Janaloka and to Brahmaloka; / and the vipra attains the nature of Brahman, O mighty-armed one, without doubt.

1.2.s:
śatānīka uvāca
brahmatvaṃ nāma duṣprāpaṃ brahmalokeṣu suvrata . . 139
1.2.d:
शतानीक उवाच
ब्रह्मत्वं नाम दुष्प्रापं ब्रह्मलोकेषु सुव्रत ॥ 139
1.2.m: Śatānīka said: / Attainment of Brahman is indeed difficult to reach among the worlds of Brahmā, O one of good vows.

1.2.s:
brahmatvaṃ kīdṛśaṃ vipro brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati .
nāmamātro'tha kiṃ vipro brahmatvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ sadā . .
yāti brahmanguṇāḥ ke syurbrahmaprāptau mamocyatām . . 1.2.140
1.2.d:
ब्रह्मत्वं कीदृशं विप्रो ब्रह्मलोकं च गच्छति ।
नाममात्रोऽथ किं विप्रो ब्रह्मत्वं ब्रह्मणः सदा ॥
याति ब्रह्मन्गुणाः के स्युर्ब्रह्मप्राप्तौ ममोच्यताम् ॥ 1.2.140
1.2.m: Of what kind is that attainment of Brahman, and does the vipra go to Brahmaloka? / Or does a vipra merely in name always attain the Brahman-hood of Brahmā? / O brāhmaṇa, what qualities are required for the attainment of Brahman? Tell me.

1.2.s:
sumanturuvāca
sādhusādhu mahābāho śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ . . 141
1.2.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
साधुसाधु महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः ॥ 141
1.2.m: Sumantu said: / Excellent, excellent, O mighty-armed one! Listen to my supreme word.

1.2.s:
ye proktā vedaśāstreṣu saṃskārā brāhmaṇasya tu .
garbhādhānādayo ye ca 1 saṃskārā yasya pārthiva . . 142
catvāriṃśatathāṣṭau ca nirvṛttāḥ śāstrato nṛpa .
sa yāti brahmaṇaḥ sthānaṃ brāhmaṇatvaṃ ca mānada 1 ..
1.2.d:
ये प्रोक्ता वेदशास्त्रेषु संस्कारा ब्राह्मणस्य तु ।
गर्भाधानादयो ये च 1 संस्कारा यस्य पार्थिव ॥ 142
चत्वारिंशतथाष्टौ च निर्वृत्ताः शास्त्रतो नृप ।
स याति ब्रह्मणः स्थानं ब्राह्मणत्वं च मानद 1 ॥
1.2.m:
Those life-cycle rites of a brāhmaṇa that are declared in the Veda and śāstras— / the rites beginning with conception, for whomsoever they are, O king,
forty and eight performed according to the śāstras, O king, / he attains the abode of Brahmā and the status of a brāhmaṇa, O honor-giver.

1.2.s: saṃskārāḥ sarvathā heturbrahmatve nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 143
1.2.d: संस्काराः सर्वथा हेतुर्ब्रह्मत्वे नात्र संशयः ॥ 143
1.2.m: Life-cycle rites are entirely the cause of reaching Brahman; of this there is no doubt.

1.2.s:
śatānīka uvāca
saṃskārāḥ ke matā brahmanbrahmatve brāhmaṇasya tu .
śaṃsa me dvijaśārdūlaṃ kautukaṃ hi mahanmama .. 144
1.2.d:
शतानीक उवाच
संस्काराः के मता ब्रह्मन्ब्रह्मत्वे ब्राह्मणस्य तु ।
शंस मे द्विजशार्दूलं कौतुकं हि महन्मम ॥ 144
1.2.m: Śatānīka said: / Which life-cycle rites are considered [requisite] for a brāhmaṇa’s Brahman-hood, O brāhmaṇa? / Declare them to me, O tiger among the twice-born, for my curiosity is great.

1.2.s:
sumanturuvāca
sādhusādhu mahābāho śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ .
ye proktā vedaśāstreṣu saṃskārā brāhmaṇasya tu ..
manīṣibhirmahābāho śṛṇu sarvānaśeṣataḥ .. 145
1.2.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
साधुसाधु महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः ।
ये प्रोक्ता वेदशास्त्रेषु संस्कारा ब्राह्मणस्य तु ॥
मनीषिभिर्महाबाहो शृणु सर्वानशेषतः ॥ 145
1.2.m: Sumantu said: / Excellent, excellent, O mighty-armed one! Listen to my supreme word / regarding the life-cycle rites of a brāhmaṇa declared in the Veda and śāstras / by the wise, O mighty-armed one; hear all of them without omission:

1.2.s:
garbhādhānaṃ puṃsavanaṃ sīmantonnayanaṃ tathā .
jātakarmānnāśanaṃ ca cūḍopanayanaṃ 2 nṛpa .. 146
1.2.d:
गर्भाधानं पुंसवनं सीमन्तोन्नयनं तथा ।
जातकर्मान्नाशनं च चूडोपनयनं 2 नृप ॥ 146
1.2.m: Garbhādhāna, puṃsavana, and sīmantonnayana, / jātakarman, annaprāśana, tonsure, and upanayana, O king;

1.2.s:
brahmavratāni catvāri snānaṃ ca tadanantaram .
sadharmacāriṇīyogo yajñānāṃ 3 karma mānada .. 147
1.2.d:
ब्रह्मव्रतानि चत्वारि स्नानं च तदनन्तरम् ।
सधर्मचारिणीयोगो यज्ञानां 3 कर्म मानद ॥ 147
1.2.m: the four vows of the Veda, and ablution immediately thereafter, / union with a lawful wife, and the performance of the [five] sacrifices, O honor-giver.

1.2.s:
pañcānāṃ kāryamityāhurātmanaḥ śreyase nṛpa .
devapitṛmanuṣyāṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ brāhmaṇastathā .. 148
1.2.d:
पञ्चानां कार्यमित्याहुरात्मनः श्रेयसे नृप ।
देवपितृमनुष्याणां भूतानां ब्राह्मणस्तथा ॥ 148
1.2.m: They declare that [the daily five sacrifices] are to be performed for one's own welfare, O king: / for the gods, ancestors, men, beings, and the brāhmaṇa.

1.2.s:
eteṣāṃ cāṣṭakākarma pārvaṇaśrāddhameva hi .
śrāvaṇī cāgrahāyaṇī caitrī cāśvayujī tathā .. 149
1.2.d:
एतेषां चाष्टकाकर्म पार्वणश्राद्धमेव हि ।
श्रावणी चाग्रहायणी चैत्री चाश्वयुजी तथा ॥ 149
1.2.m: And of these, the aṣṭakā rites, the pārvaṇa śrāddha, / the Śrāvaṇī, Āgrahāyaṇī, Caitrī, and Āśvayujī rites.

1.2.s:
pākayajñāstathā sapta agnyādhānaṃ ca satkriyā .
agnihotraṃ tathā rājandarśaṃ ca vidhusañkṣaye .. 1.2.150
1.2.d:
पाकयज्ञास्तथा सप्त अग्न्याधानं च सत्क्रिया ।
अग्निहोत्रं तथा राजन्दर्शं च विधुसञ्क्षये ॥ 1.2.150
1.2.m: Likewise, the seven pākayajñas, and the pious rite of agnyādhāna, / the agnihotra, O king, and the darśa [sacrifice] at the disappearance of the moon,

1.2.s:
paurṇamāsaṃ ca rājendra cāturmāsyāni cāpi hi .
nirūpaṇaṃ 5 paśuvadhaṃ tathā sautrāmaṇīti ca .. 151
1.2.d:
पौर्णमासं च राजेन्द्र चातुर्मास्यानि चापि हि ।
निरूपणं 5 पशुवधं तथा सौत्रामणीति च ॥ 151
1.2.m: and the paurṇamāsa [sacrifice], O best of kings, and the cāturmāsyas, / the nirūḍhapaśubandha, and the sautrāmaṇī—

1.2.s:
haviryajñāstathā sapta teṣāṃ cāpi hi satkriyā .
agniṣṭomo'tyagniṣṭomastathokthyaḥ ṣoḍaśīṃ viduḥ ..152
1.2.d:
हविर्यज्ञास्तथा सप्त तेषां चापि हि सत्क्रिया ।
अग्निष्टोमोऽत्यग्निष्टोमस्तथोक्थ्यः षोडशीं विदुः ॥152
1.2.m: likewise the seven haviryajñas, and their pious rite; / they know the agniṣṭoma, the atyagniṣṭoma, likewise the ukthya, the ṣoḍaśin,

1.2.s:
vājapeyo'tirātraśca āptoryāmeti vai smṛtaḥ 1 .
saṃskāreṣu sthitāḥ sapta somāḥ kurukulodvaha .. 153
1.2.d:
वाजपेयोऽतिरात्रश्च आप्तोर्यामेति वै स्मृतः 1 ।
संस्कारेषु स्थिताः सप्त सोमाः कुरुकुलोद्वह ॥ 153
1.2.m: the vājapeya, the atirātra, and what is known as the āptoryāma. / These seven somas are established among the saṃskāras, O sustainer of the Kuru lineage.

1.2.s:
ityete dvijasaṃskārāścatvāriṃśannṛpottama .
aṣṭau cātmaguṇāstāta śṛṇu tānapi bhārata .. 154
1.2.d:
इत्येते द्विजसंस्काराश्चत्वारिंशन्नृपोत्तम ।
अष्टौ चात्मगुणास्तात शृणु तानपि भारत ॥ 154
1.2.m: Thus, these forty are the saṃskāras of the twice-born, O best of kings. / And the virtues of the self are eight, my dear; hear them also, O descendant of Bharata:

1.2.s:
anasūyā dayā kṣāntiranāyāsaṃ ca maṅgalam .
akārpaṇyaṃ tathā śaucamaspṛhā ca kurūdvaha .. 155
1.2.d:
अनसूया दया क्षान्तिरनायासं च मङ्गलम् ।
अकार्पण्यं तथा शौचमस्पृहा च कुरूद्वह ॥ 155
1.2.m: freedom from envy, compassion, forbearance, freedom from strain, auspicious conduct, / generosity, purity, and freedom from yearning, O sustainer of the Kurus.

1.2.s:
ya ete'ṣṭaguṇāstāta kīrtyante vai manīṣibhiḥ .
eteṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vīra śṛṇu sarvamaśeṣataḥ .. 156
1.2.d:
य एतेऽष्टगुणास्तात कीर्त्यन्ते वै मनीषिभिः ।
एतेषां लक्षणं वीर शृणु सर्वमशेषतः ॥ 156
1.2.m: These eight virtues, my dear, that are proclaimed by the wise, / hear their characteristics in their entirety, O hero:

1.2.s:
na guṇānguṇino hanti na stautyātmaguṇānapi .
prahaṣyante nānyadoṣairanasūyā prakīrtitā .. 157
1.2.d:
न गुणान्गुणिनो हन्ति न स्तौत्यात्मगुणानपि ।
प्रहष्यन्ते नान्यदोषैरनसूया प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 157
1.2.m: He does not disparage the virtues of the virtuous, nor does he praise his own virtues, / and he does not rejoice at the faults of others; this is proclaimed as freedom from envy.

1.2.s:
apare bandhuvarge vā mitre dveṣṭari vā sadā .
ātmavadvartanaṃ yatsyātsā dayā parikīrtitā .. 158
1.2.d:
अपरे बन्धुवर्गे वा मित्रे द्वेष्टरि वा सदा ।
आत्मवद्वर्तनं यत्स्यात्सा दया परिकीर्तिता ॥ 158
1.2.m: Toward a stranger, a kinsman, a friend, or an enemy at all times, / to behave as toward oneself: that is proclaimed as compassion.

1.2.s:
vācā manasi kāye ca duḥkhenotpāditena ca .
na kupyati na cāprītiḥ sā kṣamā parikīrtitā .. 159
1.2.d:
वाचा मनसि काये च दुःखेनोत्पादितेन च ।
न कुप्यति न चाप्रीतिः सा क्षमा परिकीर्तिता ॥ 159
1.2.m: When distress is caused in speech, mind, and body, / he neither becomes angry nor feels displeasure: that is proclaimed as forbearance.

1.2.s:
abhakṣyaparihāraśca saṃsargaścāpyaninditaiḥ .
ācāre ca vyavasthānaṃ śaucametatprakīrtitam .. 1.2.160
1.2.d:
अभक्ष्यपरिहारश्च संसर्गश्चाप्यनिन्दितैः ।
आचारे च व्यवस्थानं शौचमेतत्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 1.2.160
1.2.m: Refraining from forbidden food, association with the blameless, / and steadfastness in proper conduct: this is proclaimed as purity.

1.2.s:
śarīraṃ pīḍyate yena śubhenāpi ca karmaṇā .
atyantaṃ tanna kurvīta anāyāsaḥ sa ucyate .. 161
1.2.d:
शरीरं पीड्यते येन शुभेनापि च कर्मणा ।
अत्यन्तं तन्न कुर्वीत अनायासः स उच्यते ॥ 161
1.2.m: That by which the body is tormented, even by a meritorious deed, / he should not do to excess; that is called freedom from strain.

1.2.s:
praśastācaraṇaṃ nityamapraśastavivarjanam .
etaddhi maṅgalaṃ proktaṃ munibhirbrahmavādibhiḥ .. 162
1.2.d:
प्रशस्ताचरणं नित्यमप्रशस्तविवर्जनम् ।
एतद्धि मङ्गलं प्रोक्तं मुनिभिर्ब्रह्मवादिभिः ॥ 162
1.2.m: Constant practice of what is praised, and abandonment of what is not praised: / this indeed is declared to be auspicious conduct by the sages who expound the Veda.

1.2.s:
stokādapi pradātavyamadīnenāntarātmanā .
ahanyahani yatkiṃcidakārpaṇyaṃ taducyate .. 163
1.2.d:
स्तोकादपि प्रदातव्यमदीनेनान्तरात्मना ।
अहन्यहनि यत्किंचिदकार्पण्यं तदुच्यते ॥ 163
1.2.m: Even from little, one should give with a cheerful heart; / whatever [one gives] day by day, that is called generosity.

1.2.s:
yathotpannena santuṣṭaḥ svalpenāpyatha vastunā .
ahiṃsayā parasveṣu 3 sā'spṛhā parikīrtitā .. 164
1.2.d:
यथोत्पन्नेन सन्तुष्टः स्वल्पेनाप्यथ वस्तुना ।
अहिंसया परस्वेषु 3 साऽस्पृहा परिकीर्तिता ॥ 164
1.2.m: Content with whatever comes to hand, even with a very small thing, / without injury regarding the possessions of others: that is proclaimed as freedom from yearning.

1.2.s:
vapuryasya tu ityetaiḥ saṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaṃ dvijaḥ .
brahmatvamiha samprāpya brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati .. 165
1.2.d:
वपुर्यस्य तु इत्येतैः संस्कारैः संस्कृतं द्विजः ।
ब्रह्मत्वमिह सम्प्राप्य ब्रह्मलोकं च गच्छति ॥ 165
1.2.m: A twice-born whose body is refined with these saṃskāras, / having attained Brahmanhood here, goes to the world of Brahmā.

1.2.s:
vaidikaiḥ karmabhiḥ puṇyairniṣekādyairdvijanmanām .
kāryaḥ śarīrasaṃskāraḥ pāvanaḥ pretya ceha ca . . 166
1.2.d:
वैदिकैः कर्मभिः पुण्यैर्निषेकाद्यैर्द्विजन्मनाम् ।
कार्यः शरीरसंस्कारः पावनः प्रेत्य चेह च ॥ 166
1.2.m: Through sacred Vedic rites beginning with conception, / a twice-born's bodily saṃskāra should be performed, purifying both in the hereafter and here.

1.2.s:
garbhaśuddhiṃ tataḥ prāpya dharmaṃ cāśramalakṣaṇam .
yāti muktiṃ na sandehaḥ purāṇe'sminnṛpottama . . 167
1.2.d:
गर्भशुद्धिं ततः प्राप्य धर्मं चाश्रमलक्षणम् ।
याति मुक्तिं न सन्देहः पुराणेऽस्मिन्नृपोत्तम ॥ 167
1.2.m: Having then attained purification of the womb, and the duty defined by the āśramas, / he goes to liberation, there is no doubt, in this Purāṇa, O best of kings.

1.2.s:
uśanti kuruśārdūla brāhmaṇā nātra saṃśayaḥ .
1āśritānāṃ viśeṣeṇa ye nityaṃ svastivādinaḥ . . 168
1.2.d:
उशन्ति कुरुशार्दूल ब्राह्मणा नात्र संशयः ।
1आश्रितानां विशेषेण ये नित्यं स्वस्तिवादिनः ॥ 168
1.2.m: Brāhmaṇas wish it so, O tiger among the Kurus, there is no doubt in this, / especially for dependents who constantly utter blessings.

1.2.s:
nikaṭasthāndvijānhitvā yo'nyānpūjayati dvijān .
siddhaṃ pāpaṃ tadapamānāttadvaktuṃ naiva śakyate . . 169
1.2.d:
निकटस्थान्द्विजान्हित्वा योऽन्यान्पूजयति द्विजान् ।
सिद्धं पापं तदपमानात्तद्वक्तुं नैव शक्यते ॥ 169
1.2.m: He who, having passed over the twice-born residing nearby, honors other twice-born, / through their disrespect a sin is produced that cannot even be described.

1.2.s:
tasmātsadā samīpasthaḥ sampūjyo vidhivannṛpa .
pūjayedatithīṃstadvadannapānādidānataḥ . . 1.2.170
1.2.d:
तस्मात्सदा समीपस्थः सम्पूज्यो विधिवन्नृप ।
पूजयेदतिथींस्तद्वदन्नपानादिदानतः ॥ 1.2.170
1.2.m: Therefore, the one residing nearby should always be duly honored, O king; / likewise, one should honor guests with gifts of food, drink, and the like.

1.2.s:
brāhmaṇaḥ sarvavarṇānāṃ jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhastathottamaḥ .
evamasminpurāṇe tu saṃskārānbrāhmaṇasya tu . . 171
1.2.d:
ब्राह्मणः सर्ववर्णानां ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठस्तथोत्तमः ।
एवमस्मिन्पुराणे तु संस्कारान्ब्राह्मणस्य तु ॥ 171
1.2.m: The brāhmaṇa is the eldest, the most eminent, and the best of all varṇas. / Thus, in this Purāṇa, he who hears, knows,

1.2.s:
śṛṇoti yaśca jānāti yaścāpi paṭhate sadā .
ṛddhiṃ vṛddhiṃ tathā kīrtiṃ prāpyeha śriyamuttamām . . 172
1.2.d:
शृणोति यश्च जानाति यश्चापि पठते सदा ।
ऋद्धिं वृद्धिं तथा कीर्तिं प्राप्येह श्रियमुत्तमाम् ॥ 172
1.2.m: and also constantly recites the saṃskāras of a brāhmaṇa, / having attained prosperity, growth, and fame, and supreme fortune here,

1.2.s:
dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ yaśaścāpi putrānbandhūnsurūpatām .
sāvitraṃ lokamāsādya brahmalokamavāpnuyāt . . 173
iti śrībhaviṣya mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ
brāhme parvaṇi dvitīyo'dhyāyaḥ . 2 .
garbhādhānādārabhya samāsātsarvasaṃskāravarṇanamācamanādividhivarṇanañca
1.2.d:
धनं धान्यं यशश्चापि पुत्रान्बन्धून्सुरूपताम् ।
सावित्रं लोकमासाद्य ब्रह्मलोकमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 173
इति श्रीभविष्य महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां
ब्राह्मे पर्वणि द्वितीयोऽध्यायः । 2 ।
गर्भाधानादारभ्य समासात्सर्वसंस्कारवर्णनमाचमनादिविधिवर्णनञ्च
1.2.m:
wealth, grain, renown, sons, relatives, and good looks, / reaching the world of Savitṛ, he attains the world of Brahmā.
Thus ends the second chapter in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty thousand [verses].
A concise description of all the saṃskāras beginning with garbhādhāna, and the description of the rules of sipping water and so forth.

1.3.s:
śatānīka uvāca
jātakarmādisaṃskārānvarṇānāmanupūrvaśaḥ .
āśramāṇāṃ ca me dharmaṃ kathayasva dvijottama . . 1
1.3.d:
शतानीक उवाच
जातकर्मादिसंस्कारान्वर्णानामनुपूर्वशः ।
आश्रमाणां च मे धर्मं कथयस्व द्विजोत्तम ॥ 1
1.3.m: Śatānīka said: / Explain to me in regular order, O best of the twice-born, / the saṃskāras of the varṇas beginning with jātakarma, and the duties of the āśramas.

1.3.s:
sumanturuvāca
garbhādhānaṃ puṃsavanaṃ sīmantonnayanaṃ tathā .
jātakarmānnaprāśaśca cūḍāmauñjīnibandhanam . . 2
1.3.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
गर्भाधानं पुंसवनं सीमन्तोन्नयनं तथा ।
जातकर्मान्नप्राशश्च चूडामौञ्जीनिबन्धनम् ॥ 2
1.3.m: Sumantu said: / The garbhādhāna, the puṃsavana, and likewise the sīmantonnayana, / the jātakarma, the annaprāśana, the cūḍā, and the tying of the mauñjī [girdle].

1.3.s:
baijikaṃ gārbhikaṃ caino dvijānāmapamṛjyate .
svādhyāyena vratairhomaistraividyenejyayā śrutaiḥ . . 3
1.3.d:
बैजिकं गार्भिकं चैनो द्विजानामपमृज्यते ।
स्वाध्यायेन व्रतैर्होमैस्त्रैविद्येनेज्यया श्रुतैः ॥ 3
1.3.m: The sin arising from the seed and from the womb is wiped away for the twice-born / by Vedic recitation, vows, burnt offerings, the triple Veda, worship, and Vedic studies,

1.3.s:
mahāyajñaiśca brāhmīyaṃ yajñaiśca kriyate tanuḥ .
śṛṇuṣvaikamanā rājanyathā sā kriyate tanuḥ . . 4
1.3.d:
महायज्ञैश्च ब्राह्मीयं यज्ञैश्च क्रियते तनुः ।
शृणुष्वैकमना राजन्यथा सा क्रियते तनुः ॥ 4
1.3.m: and by the great sacrifices; and this body is made divine by sacrifices. / Listen attentively, O king, to how that body is so transformed:

1.3.s:
prāṅnābhikartanātpuṃso jātakarma vidhīyate .
mantravatprāśanaṃ cāsya hiraṇyamadhusarpiṣām . . 5
1.3.d:
प्राङ्नाभिकर्तनात्पुंसो जातकर्म विधीयते ।
मन्त्रवत्प्राशनं चास्य हिरण्यमधुसर्पिषाम् ॥ 5
1.3.m: Before the cutting of the navel cord, the jātakarma is prescribed for a male; / and feeding him gold, honey, and ghee with mantras.

1.3.s:
nāmadheyaṃ daśamyāṃ tu kecidicchanti pārthiva .
dvādaśyāmapare rājanmāsi pūrṇe tathā pare . . 6
1.3.d:
नामधेयं दशम्यां तु केचिदिच्छन्ति पार्थिव ।
द्वादश्यामपरे राजन्मासि पूर्णे तथा परे ॥ 6
1.3.m: Some desire the name-giving rite on the tenth day, O king, / others on the twelfth day, O king, and others when a full month has passed;

1.3.s:
aṣṭādaśe'hani tathā'nye vadanti manīṣiṇaḥ .
puṇye tithau muhūrte ca nakṣatre ca guṇānvite . . 7
1.3.d:
अष्टादशेऽहनि तथाऽन्ये वदन्ति मनीषिणः ।
पुण्ये तिथौ मुहूर्ते च नक्षत्रे च गुणान्विते ॥ 7
1.3.m: and other wise men declare it to be on the eighteenth day, / on an auspicious lunar day, muhūrta, and lunar asterism endowed with good qualities.

1.3.s:
maṅgalyaṃ tāta viprasya śivaśarmeti pārthiva .
rājanyasya viśiṣṭaṃ 1 tu induvarmeti kathyate 2 . .. 8 ..
1.3.d:
मङ्गल्यं तात विप्रस्य शिवशर्मेति पार्थिव ।
राजन्यस्य विशिष्टं 1 तु इन्दुवर्मेति कथ्यते 2 ॥। 8 ॥
1.3.m: For a vipra it should be auspicious, O dear one, such as 'Śivaśarman', O king; / for a rājanya it is prescribed to be distinguished, called 'Induvarman';

1.3.s:
vaiśyasya dhanasaṃyuktaṃ śūdrasya ca jugupsitam .
dhanavardhaneti vaiśyasya sarvadāseti hīnaje . . 9
1.3.d:
वैश्यस्य धनसंयुक्तं शूद्रस्य च जुगुप्सितम् ।
धनवर्धनेति वैश्यस्य सर्वदासेति हीनजे ॥ 9
1.3.m: for a vaiśya it should be connected with wealth, and for a śūdra contemptible; / 'Dhanavardhana' for a vaiśya, and 'Sarvadāsa' for one of low birth.

1.3.s:
manunā ca tathā proktaṃ nāmno lakṣaṇamuttamam .
śarmavadbrāhmaṇasya syādrājño rakṣāsamanvitam . . 1.3.10
1.3.d:
मनुना च तथा प्रोक्तं नाम्नो लक्षणमुत्तमम् ।
शर्मवद्ब्राह्मणस्य स्याद्राज्ञो रक्षासमन्वितम् ॥ 1.3.10
1.3.m: And likewise, the excellent characteristic of a name was declared by Manu: / for a brāhmaṇa it should denote comfort, for a king it should denote protection;

1.3.s:
vaiśyasya puṣṭisaṃyuktaṃ śūdrasya preṣyasaṃyutam .
strīṇāṃ sukhodyamakrūraṃ vispaṣṭārthamanoramam . . 11
1.3.d:
वैश्यस्य पुष्टिसंयुक्तं शूद्रस्य प्रेष्यसंयुतम् ।
स्त्रीणां सुखोद्यमक्रूरं विस्पष्टार्थमनोरमम् ॥ 11
1.3.m: for a vaiśya it should be connected with prosperity, for a śūdra connected with service. / For women, it should be easy to pronounce, gentle, of clear meaning, pleasing,

1.3.s:
maṅgalyaṃ dīrghavarṇāntamāśīrvādābhidhānavat .
dvādaśe'hani rājendra śiśorniṣkamaṇaṃ gṛhāt . . 12
1.3.d:
मङ्गल्यं दीर्घवर्णान्तमाशीर्वादाभिधानवत् ।
द्वादशेऽहनि राजेन्द्र शिशोर्निष्कमणं गृहात् ॥ 12
1.3.m: auspicious, ending in a long vowel, and containing a blessing. / On the twelfth day, O best of kings, the infant's departure from the house [takes place];

1.3.s:
caturthe māsi karttavyaṃ tathānyeṣāṃ mataṃ vibho .
ṣaṣṭhe'nnaprāśanaṃ māsi yatheṣṭaṃ maṅgalaṃ kule . . 13
1.3.d:
चतुर्थे मासि कर्त्तव्यं तथान्येषां मतं विभो ।
षष्ठेऽन्नप्राशनं मासि यथेष्टं मङ्गलं कुले ॥ 13
1.3.m: or in the fourth month it should be done, according to the opinion of others, O lord; / in the sixth month the first feeding of grain [takes place], with whatever auspicious rite is desired in the family.

1.3.s:
cūḍākarma dvijātīnāṃ sarveṣāmanupūrvaśaḥ .
prathame'bde tṛtīye vā kartavyaṃ kurunandana . . 14
1.3.d:
चूडाकर्म द्विजातीनां सर्वेषामनुपूर्वशः ।
प्रथमेऽब्दे तृतीये वा कर्तव्यं कुरुनन्दन ॥ 14
1.3.m: The tonsure rite for all the twice-born classes in regular order / should be performed in the first year or the third, O delight of the Kurus.

1.3.s:
garbhāṣṭame'bde kurvīta brāhmaṇasyopanāyanam .
garbhādekādaśe rājankṣatriyasya vinirdiśet . . 15
1.3.d:
गर्भाष्टमेऽब्दे कुर्वीत ब्राह्मणस्योपनायनम् ।
गर्भादेकादशे राजन्क्षत्रियस्य विनिर्दिशेत् ॥ 15
1.3.m: One should perform the initiation of a brāhmaṇa in the eighth year from conception; / for a kṣatriya, O king, one should prescribe it in the eleventh from conception;

1.3.s:
dvādaśe'bde'pi garbhāttu vaiśyasya vratamādiśet .
brahmavarcasakāmena kāryaṃ viprasya pañcame . . 16
1.3.d:
द्वादशेऽब्देऽपि गर्भात्तु वैश्यस्य व्रतमादिशेत् ।
ब्रह्मवर्चसकामेन कार्यं विप्रस्य पञ्चमे ॥ 16
1.3.m: and for a vaiśya one should prescribe the vow in the twelfth year from conception. / For one desiring sacred radiance, it should be performed for a vipra in the fifth,

1.3.s:
balārthinā tathā rājñaḥ ṣaṣṭhe 'bde kāryameva hi .
arthakāmena vaiśyasya aṣṭame kurunandana . . 17
1.3.d:
बलार्थिना तथा राज्ञः षष्ठे ऽब्दे कार्यमेव हि ।
अर्थकामेन वैश्यस्य अष्टमे कुरुनन्दन ॥ 17
1.3.m: for a king desiring power, it should indeed be done in the sixth year, / and for a vaiśya desiring wealth, in the eighth, O delight of the Kurus.

1.3.s:
āṣoḍaśādbrāhmaṇasya sāvitrī nātivartate .
dvāviṃśateḥ kṣatrabandhorācaturviṃśaterviśaḥ . . 18
1.3.d:
आषोडशाद्ब्राह्मणस्य सावित्री नातिवर्तते ।
द्वाविंशतेः क्षत्रबन्धोराचतुर्विंशतेर्विशः ॥ 18
1.3.m: Up to the sixteenth year, the Sāvitrī does not elapse for a brāhmaṇa; / up to the twenty-second for a base kṣatriya, up to the twenty-fourth for a vaiśya.

1.3.s:
ata ūrdhvaṃ tu ye rājanyathākālamasaṃskṛtāḥ .
sāvitrīpatitā vrātyā vrātyastomādṛte 3 kratoḥ . . 19
1.3.d:
अत ऊर्ध्वं तु ये राजन्यथाकालमसंस्कृताः ।
सावित्रीपतिता व्रात्या व्रात्यस्तोमादृते 3 क्रतोः ॥ 19
1.3.m: Beyond that, those who are not consecrated at the proper time, O king, / fallen from the Sāvitrī, become vrātyas, except through the vrātyastoma sacrifice.

1.3.s:
na cāpyebhirapūtaistu āpadyapi hi karhicit .
brāhmaṃ yaunaṃ ca sambandhamācaredbrāhmaṇaiḥ saha . . 1.3.20
1.3.d:
न चाप्येभिरपूतैस्तु आपद्यपि हि कर्हिचित् ।
ब्राह्मं यौनं च सम्बन्धमाचरेद्ब्राह्मणैः सह ॥ 1.3.20
1.3.m: Nor should one ever, even in times of distress, / enter into an alliance of Vedic study or marriage through brāhmaṇas with these unpurified men.

1.3.s:
bhavanti rājaṃścarmāṇi vratināṃ trividhāni ca .
kārṣṇarauravavāstāni brahmakṣatraviśāṃ nṛpa . . 21
1.3.d:
भवन्ति राजंश्चर्माणि व्रतिनां त्रिविधानि च ।
कार्ष्णरौरववास्तानि ब्रह्मक्षत्रविशां नृप ॥ 21
1.3.m: O king, the skins for those observing vows are threefold: / of black antelope, ruru deer, and goat, O ruler of men, for brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas.

1.3.s:
vaśīraṃścānupūrvyeṇa vastrāṇi vividhāni tu .
brahmakṣatraviśo rājañchāṇakṣaumādikāni ca . . 22
1.3.d:
वशीरंश्चानुपूर्व्येण वस्त्राणि विविधानि तु ।
ब्रह्मक्षत्रविशो राजञ्छाणक्षौमादिकानि च ॥ 22
1.3.m: And their garments in order are varied: / hempen, flaxen, and the like, O king, for brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas.

1.3.s:
mauñjī trivṛtsamā ślakṣṇā kāryā viprasya mekhalā .
kṣatriyasya ca maurvījyā vaiśyasya śaṇatāntavī . . 23
1.3.d:
मौञ्जी त्रिवृत्समा श्लक्ष्णा कार्या विप्रस्य मेखला ।
क्षत्रियस्य च मौर्वीज्या वैश्यस्य शणतान्तवी ॥ 23
1.3.m: The girdle of a brāhmaṇa should be made of muñja grass, threefold, even, and smooth; / of a kṣatriya, a bowstring of mūrvā grass; and of a vaiśya, woven of hempen threads.

1.3.s:
muñjālābhe tu kartavyā kuśāśmantakabalvajaiḥ .
trivṛttā granthinaikena tribhiḥ pañcabhireva ca . . 24
1.3.d:
मुञ्जालाभे तु कर्तव्या कुशाश्मन्तकबल्वजैः ।
त्रिवृत्ता ग्रन्थिनैकेन त्रिभिः पञ्चभिरेव च ॥ 24
1.3.m: In the absence of muñja grass, it should be made of kuśa, aśmantaka, or balvaja grass, / threefold, with one knot, or with three or five.

1.3.s:
kārpāsamupavītaṃ syādviprasyordhvavṛtaṃ trivṛt .
śaṇasūtramayaṃ rājño vaiśyasyāvikasautrikam . . 25
1.3.d:
कार्पासमुपवीतं स्याद्विप्रस्योर्ध्ववृतं त्रिवृत् ।
शणसूत्रमयं राज्ञो वैश्यस्याविकसौत्रिकम् ॥ 25
1.3.m: The sacred thread of a brāhmaṇa should be of cotton, twisted upward, threefold; / of a king, made of hempen thread; of a vaiśya, of woolen thread.

1.3.s:
puṣkarāṇi tathā caiṣāṃ bhavanti trividhāni tu .
brahmaṇo bailvapālāśau tṛtīyaṃ plakṣajaṃ nṛpa . . 26
1.3.d:
पुष्कराणि तथा चैषां भवन्ति त्रिविधानि तु ।
ब्रह्मणो बैल्वपालाशौ तृतीयं प्लक्षजं नृप ॥ 26
1.3.m: And their staffs also are of three kinds: / for a brāhmaṇa, made of bilva and palāśa, and a third from plakṣa, O king;

1.3.s:
vāṭakhādirau kṣatriyastu tathānyaṃ vetasodbhavam .
pailavodumbarau vaiśyastathāśvatthajameva hi . . 27
1.3.d:
वाटखादिरौ क्षत्रियस्तु तथान्यं वेतसोद्भवम् ।
पैलवोदुम्बरौ वैश्यस्तथाश्वत्थजमेव हि ॥ 27
1.3.m: A kṣatriya's of banyan and khadira, and another originating from cane; / a vaiśya's of pīlu and udumbara, and likewise indeed from aśvattha.

1.3.s:
daṇḍānetānmahābāho dharmato'rhanti dhāritum .
keśāntiko brāhmaṇasya daṇḍaḥ kāryaḥ pramāṇataḥ . . 28
1.3.d:
दण्डानेतान्महाबाहो धर्मतोऽर्हन्ति धारितुम् ।
केशान्तिको ब्राह्मणस्य दण्डः कार्यः प्रमाणतः ॥ 28
1.3.m: O mighty-armed one, according to dharma they ought to carry these staffs. / By measure, the staff of a brāhmaṇa should reach to the ends of his hair;

1.3.s:
lalāṭasammito rājñaḥ syāttu nāsāntiko viśaḥ .
ṛjavaste tū sarve syurbrāhmaṇāḥ saumyadarśanāḥ . . 29
1.3.d:
ललाटसम्मितो राज्ञः स्यात्तु नासान्तिको विशः ।
ऋजवस्ते तू सर्वे स्युर्ब्राह्मणाः सौम्यदर्शनाः ॥ 29
1.3.m: A king's should equal his forehead, but a vaiśya's should reach to the tip of his nose. / They should all be straight, pleasant in appearance for brāhmaṇas,

1.3.s:
anudvegakarā nṝṇāṃ satvaco nāgnidūṣitāḥ .
pragṛhya cepsitaṃ daṇḍamupasthāya ca bhāskaram . . 1.3.30
1.3.d:
अनुद्वेगकरा नॄणां सत्वचो नाग्निदूषिताः ।
प्रगृह्य चेप्सितं दण्डमुपस्थाय च भास्करम् ॥ 1.3.30
1.3.m: Not frightening to men, with their bark intact, and not damaged by fire. / Having taken the desired staff and stood facing the sun,

1.3.s:
samyagguruṃ tathā pūjya caredbhaikṣyaṃ yathāvidhi .
bhavatpūrvaṃ caredbhaikṣyamupanīto dvijottamaḥ . . 31
1.3.d:
सम्यग्गुरुं तथा पूज्य चरेद्भैक्ष्यं यथाविधि ।
भवत्पूर्वं चरेद्भैक्ष्यमुपनीतो द्विजोत्तमः ॥ 31
1.3.m: And having duly worshipped the teacher, he should wander for alms according to rule. / The initiated best of the twice-born should wander for alms [putting the word] 'bhavat' first;

1.3.s:
bhavanmadhyaṃ tu rājanyo vaiśyasya bhavaduttaram .
mātaraṃ vā svasāraṃ vā māturvā bhaginīṃ nijām . . 32
1.3.d:
भवन्मध्यं तु राजन्यो वैश्यस्य भवदुत्तरम् ।
मातरं वा स्वसारं वा मातुर्वा भगिनीं निजाम् ॥ 32
1.3.m: A kṣatriya with 'bhavat' in the middle, but a vaiśya with 'bhavat' at the end. / From his mother, or his sister, or his mother's own sister,

1.3.s:
bhikṣeta bhaikṣyaṃ prathamaṃ yā cainaṃ nāvamānayet .
suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ cānnaṃ sā pātre'sya vinirdiśet . . 33
1.3.d:
भिक्षेत भैक्ष्यं प्रथमं या चैनं नावमानयेत् ।
सुवर्णं रजतं चान्नं सा पात्रेऽस्य विनिर्दिशेत् ॥ 33
1.3.m: He should first beg alms, [or from one] who would not dishonour him. / Gold, silver, and food she should place into his bowl.

1.3.s:
samāhṛtya tato bhaikṣyaṃ yāvadarthamamāyayā .
nivedya gurave'śnīyādācamya prāṅmukhaḥ śuciḥ . . 34
1.3.d:
समाहृत्य ततो भैक्ष्यं यावदर्थममायया ।
निवेद्य गुरवेऽश्नीयादाचम्य प्राङ्मुखः शुचिः ॥ 34
1.3.m: Then having collected alms as much as needed without deceit, / and offering it to his teacher, he should eat, pure, having sipped water, facing east.

1.3.s:
āyuṣyaṃ prāṅmukho bhuṅkte yaśasyaṃ dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ .
śriyaṃ pratyaṅmukho bhuṅkte ṛtaṃ 1 bhuṅkte udaṅmukhaḥ . . 35
1.3.d:
आयुष्यं प्राङ्मुखो भुङ्क्ते यशस्यं दक्षिणामुखः ।
श्रियं प्रत्यङ्मुखो भुङ्क्ते ऋतं 1 भुङ्क्ते उदङ्मुखः ॥ 35
1.3.m: Facing east he eats for longevity; facing south, for renown; / facing west he eats for prosperity; facing north he eats for truth.

1.3.s:
upaspṛśya dvijo rājannannamadyātsamāhitaḥ .
bhuktvā copaspṛśetsamyagadbhiḥ khāni ca saṃspṛśet . . 36
1.3.d:
उपस्पृश्य द्विजो राजन्नन्नमद्यात्समाहितः ।
भुक्त्वा चोपस्पृशेत्सम्यगद्भिः खानि च संस्पृशेत् ॥ 36
1.3.m: Having sipped water, O king, a twice-born should eat food with a composed mind; / and having eaten, he should properly sip water and touch the bodily apertures with water.

1.3.s:
tathānnaṃ pūjayennityamadyāccaitadakutsayan .
darśanāttasya haṣyedvai prasīdeccāpi bhārata. . 37
1.3.d:
तथान्नं पूजयेन्नित्यमद्याच्चैतदकुत्सयन् ।
दर्शनात्तस्य हष्येद्वै प्रसीदेच्चापि भारत॥ 37
1.3.m: Likewise, he should always venerate his food and eat it without reviling it; / seeing it, he should indeed rejoice and be pleased, O descendant of Bharata.

1.3.s:
abhinandya tato'śnīyādityevaṃ manurabravīt .
pūjitaṃ tvaśanaṃ nityaṃ balamojaśca yacchati. . 38
1.3.d:
अभिनन्द्य ततोऽश्नीयादित्येवं मनुरब्रवीत् ।
पूजितं त्वशनं नित्यं बलमोजश्च यच्छति॥ 38
1.3.m: Then, having welcomed it, he should eat: thus Manu has declared. / For food that is venerated always gives strength and vigour;

1.3.s:
apūjitaṃ tu tadbhuktamubhayaṃ nāśayedidam 6.
nocchiṣṭaṃ kasyaciddadyānnādyāccaitattathāntarā . . 39
1.3.d:
अपूजितं तु तद्भुक्तमुभयं नाशयेदिदम् 6.
नोच्छिष्टं कस्यचिद्दद्यान्नाद्याच्चैतत्तथान्तरा ॥ 39
1.3.m: Eaten without veneration, however, it destroys both of these. / He should not give leftovers to anyone, nor should he eat while interrupting [the meal].

1.3.s:
yastvannamantarā kṛtvā lobhādatti nṛpottama .
vināśaṃ yāti sa nara iha loke paratra ca . .
yathābhavatpurā vaiśyo dhanavarddhanasaṃjñitaḥ . . 1.3.40
1.3.d:
यस्त्वन्नमन्तरा कृत्वा लोभादत्ति नृपोत्तम ।
विनाशं याति स नर इह लोके परत्र च ॥
यथाभवत्पुरा वैश्यो धनवर्द्धनसंज्ञितः ॥ 1.3.40
1.3.m: The man who, out of greed, eats after having interrupted his food, O best of kings, / goes to ruin in this world and in the next, / just as happened of old to the vaiśya named Dhanavardhana.

1.3.s:
śatānīka uvāca
sa kathamantaraṃ pūrvamannasya dvijasattama .
kimantaraṃ tathānnasya kathaṃ vā tatkṛtaṃ bhavet . . 41
1.3.d:
शतानीक उवाच
स कथमन्तरं पूर्वमन्नस्य द्विजसत्तम ।
किमन्तरं तथान्नस्य कथं वा तत्कृतं भवेत् ॥ 41
1.3.m: Śatānīka said: / How did he interrupt his food formerly, O best of the twice-born? / What is an interruption of food, or how does it occur?

1.3.s:
sumanturuvāca
purā kṛtayuge rājanvaiśyo vasati puṣkare .
dhanavardhananāmā vai samṛddhau dhanadhānyataḥ . . 42
1.3.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
पुरा कृतयुगे राजन्वैश्यो वसति पुष्करे ।
धनवर्धननामा वै समृद्धौ धनधान्यतः ॥ 42
1.3.m: Sumantu said: / Formerly in the Kṛta age, O king, a vaiśya lived at Puṣkara, / named Dhanavardhana indeed, prosperous with wealth and grain.

1.3.s:
nidāghakāle rājendra sa kṛtvā vaiśvadevikam .
saputrabhrātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ tathā vai mitrabandhubhiḥ . .
āhāraṃ kurute rājanbhakṣyabhojyasamanvitam 1 . . 43
1.3.d:
निदाघकाले राजेन्द्र स कृत्वा वैश्वदेविकम् ।
सपुत्रभ्रातृभिः सार्धं तथा वै मित्रबन्धुभिः ॥
आहारं कुरुते राजन्भक्ष्यभोज्यसमन्वितम् 1 ॥ 43
1.3.m: In the hot season, O king of kings, having performed the Vaiśvadeva rite / along with his sons and brothers, as well as friends and kin, / he took his meal, O king, consisting of foods to chew and eat.

1.3.s:
atha tadbhuñjatastasya 2 annaṃ śabdo mahānabhūt .
karuṇaḥ kuruśārdūla atha taṃ sa pradhāvitaḥ . . 44
1.3.d:
अथ तद्भुञ्जतस्तस्य 2 अन्नं शब्दो महानभूत् ।
करुणः कुरुशार्दूल अथ तं स प्रधावितः ॥ 44
1.3.m: Then, as he was eating that food, a great sound arose, / pitiful, O tiger among the Kurus; then he ran toward it.

1.3.s:
tyaktvā sa bhojanaṃ yāvanniṣkrānto gṛhabāhyataḥ .
atha śabdastirobhūtaḥ sa bhūyo gṛhamāgataḥ . . 45
1.3.d:
त्यक्त्वा स भोजनं यावन्निष्क्रान्तो गृहबाह्यतः ।
अथ शब्दस्तिरोभूतः स भूयो गृहमागतः ॥ 45
1.3.m: Leaving his meal, as soon as he went outside the house, / the sound vanished; he returned again to the house.

1.3.s:
tameva bhājanaṃ gṛhya 3 āhāraṃ kṛtavānnṛpa .
bhuktaśeṣaṃ mahābāho āhāraṃ sa tu bhuktavān . . 46
1.3.d:
तमेव भाजनं गृह्य 3 आहारं कृतवान्नृप ।
भुक्तशेषं महाबाहो आहारं स तु भुक्तवान् ॥ 46
1.3.m: Taking that very dish, O king, he took his food; / O mighty-armed one, he ate the remainder of what had been eaten.

1.3.s:
bhuktvā sa śatadhā jātastasminneva kṣaṇe nṛpa .
tasmādannaṃ na rājendra aśnīyādantarā kvacit . . 47
1.3.d:
भुक्त्वा स शतधा जातस्तस्मिन्नेव क्षणे नृप ।
तस्मादन्नं न राजेन्द्र अश्नीयादन्तरा क्वचित् ॥ 47
1.3.m: Having eaten, he burst into a hundred pieces at that very moment, O king. / Therefore, O king of kings, one should never eat food with an interruption.

1.3.s:
na caivātyaśanaṃ kuryānna cocchiṣṭaḥ kvacidvrajet .
raso bhavatyatyaśanādrasādrogaḥ pravartate . . 48
1.3.d:
न चैवात्यशनं कुर्यान्न चोच्छिष्टः क्वचिद्व्रजेत् ।
रसो भवत्यत्यशनाद्रसाद्रोगः प्रवर्तते ॥ 48
1.3.m: Nor should one overeat, nor should one go anywhere while impure with leftovers. / Chyle arises from overeating; from [defective] chyle, disease sets in.

1.3.s:
snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ pitṛdevābhipūjanam .
na bhavanti rase jāte narāṇāṃ bharatarṣabha . . 49
1.3.d:
स्नानं दानं जपो होमः पितृदेवाभिपूजनम् ।
न भवन्ति रसे जाते नराणां भरतर्षभ ॥ 49
1.3.m: Bathing, giving, recitation, oblation, and worship of the ancestors and deities / do not take place for men when [excess] chyle is produced, O bull of the Bharatas.

1.3.s:
anārogyamanāyuṣyamasvargyaṃ cātibhojanam .
apuṇyaṃ lokavidviṣṭaṃ tasmāttatparivarjayet . . 1.3.50
1.3.d:
अनारोग्यमनायुष्यमस्वर्ग्यं चातिभोजनम् ।
अपुण्यं लोकविद्विष्टं तस्मात्तत्परिवर्जयेत् ॥ 1.3.50
1.3.m: Overeating is unwholesome, harmful to longevity, obstructive to heaven, / devoid of merit, and hated by the world; therefore, one should avoid it.

1.3.s:
yakṣabhūtapiśācānāṃ rakṣasāṃ ca nṛpottama .
4gamyo bhavati vai vipra ucchiṣṭo nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 51
1.3.d:
यक्षभूतपिशाचानां रक्षसां च नृपोत्तम ।
4गम्यो भवति वै विप्र उच्छिष्टो नात्र संशयः ॥ 51
1.3.m: To yakṣas, ghosts, piśācas, and rākṣasas, O best of kings, / a twice-born impure with leftovers becomes accessible; of this there is no doubt.

1.3.s:
śucitvamāśrayettasmācchucitvānmodate diti? .
sukhena ceha ramate itīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ . . 52
1.3.d:
शुचित्वमाश्रयेत्तस्माच्छुचित्वान्मोदते दिति? ।
सुखेन चेह रमते इतीयं वैदिकी श्रुतिः ॥ 52
1.3.m: Therefore, one should resort to purity; because of purity, [even] Diti rejoices / and delights in happiness here—such is the Vedic revelation.

1.3.s:
śatānīka uvāca
śucitāmiyātkathaṃ vipraḥ kathaṃ cāśucitāmiyāt .
etanme ihi viprendra kautukaṃ paramaṃ mama . . 53
1.3.d:
शतानीक उवाच
शुचितामियात्कथं विप्रः कथं चाशुचितामियात् ।
एतन्मे इहि विप्रेन्द्र कौतुकं परमं मम ॥ 53
1.3.m: Śatānīka said: / How would a twice-born attain purity, and how would he incur impurity? / Tell me this, O chief of the twice-born; it is my great curiosity.

1.3.s:
sumanturuvāca
upaspṛśya śucirvipro bhavate bharatarṣabha .
vidhivatkuruśārdūla bhavedvidhiparo hyataḥ . . 54
1.3.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
उपस्पृश्य शुचिर्विप्रो भवते भरतर्षभ ।
विधिवत्कुरुशार्दूल भवेद्विधिपरो ह्यतः ॥ 54
1.3.m: Sumantu said: / Having sipped water, a twice-born becomes pure, O bull of the Bharatas, / according to rule, O tiger among the Kurus; he should therefore be intent upon the rule.

1.3.s:
śatānīka uvāca
upasparśavidhiṃ vipra kathaya tvaṃ mamākhilam .
śucitvamāpnuyādyena ācānto brāhmaṇo dvijaḥ . . 55
1.3.d:
शतानीक उवाच
उपस्पर्शविधिं विप्र कथय त्वं ममाखिलम् ।
शुचित्वमाप्नुयाद्येन आचान्तो ब्राह्मणो द्विजः ॥ 55
1.3.m: Śatānīka said: / O twice-born, tell me the entire rule of sipping water, / by which a brāhmaṇa twice-born, having sipped, would attain purity.

1.3.s:
sumanturuvāca
sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi rājendra śṛṇu vipro yathā bhavet .
śucirbharataśārdūla vidhinā yena vā vibho . . 56
1.3.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
साधु पृष्टोऽस्मि राजेन्द्र शृणु विप्रो यथा भवेत् ।
शुचिर्भरतशार्दूल विधिना येन वा विभो ॥ 56
1.3.m: Sumantu said: / I am well questioned, O king of kings! Hear how a twice-born becomes / pure, O tiger of the Bharatas, and by which rule, O lord.

1.3.s:
prakṣālya hastau pādau ca prāṅmukhodaṅmukho'pi vā .
upaviśya śucau deśe bāhuṃ kṛtvā ca dakṣiṇam . . 57
1.3.d:
प्रक्षाल्य हस्तौ पादौ च प्राङ्मुखोदङ्मुखोऽपि वा ।
उपविश्य शुचौ देशे बाहुं कृत्वा च दक्षिणम् ॥ 57
1.3.m: Having washed both hands and feet, facing east or north, / seated in a pure place, and placing the right arm

1.3.s:
jānvantare mahābāho brahmasūtrasamanvitaḥ 1 .
susamau caraṇau kṛtvā tathā baddhaśikho nṛpa . . 58
1.3.d:
जान्वन्तरे महाबाहो ब्रह्मसूत्रसमन्वितः 1 ।
सुसमौ चरणौ कृत्वा तथा बद्धशिखो नृप ॥ 58
1.3.m: Between the knees, O mighty-armed one, equipped with the sacred thread, / having made both feet well-aligned, and having his topknot bound, O king,

1.3.s:
na tiṣṭhanna ca saṃjalpaṃstathā cānavalokayan .
na tvarankupito vāpi tyaktvā rājansudūrataḥ . . 59
1.3.d:
न तिष्ठन्न च संजल्पंस्तथा चानवलोकयन् ।
न त्वरन्कुपितो वापि त्यक्त्वा राजन्सुदूरतः ॥ 59
1.3.m: Not standing, not chattering, and not looking around, / not hurrying or angry, having cast [distractions] far away, O king,

1.3.s:
prasannābhistathādbhistu ācāntaḥ śucitāmiyāt .
noṣṇābhirna saphenābhiryuktābhiḥ kaluṣeṇa ca . . 1.3.60
1.3.d:
प्रसन्नाभिस्तथाद्भिस्तु आचान्तः शुचितामियात् ।
नोष्णाभिर्न सफेनाभिर्युक्ताभिः कलुषेण च ॥ 1.3.60
1.3.m: Having sipped with clear water, he would attain purity; / not with hot water, nor with frothy water, nor with [water] accompanied by turbidity,

1.3.s:
varṇena rasagandhābhyāṃ hīnābhirna ca bhārata .
sabudbudābhiśca tathā nācāmetpaṇḍito nṛpa . . 61
1.3.d:
वर्णेन रसगन्धाभ्यां हीनाभिर्न च भारत ।
सबुद्बुदाभिश्च तथा नाचामेत्पण्डितो नृप ॥ 61
1.3.m: Nor devoid of [natural] colour, taste, and smell, O descendant of Bharata; / nor with water full of bubbles should a wise man sip, O king.

1.3.s:
pañcatīrthāni viprasya śrūyante dakṣiṇe kare .
devatīrthaṃ pitṛtīrthaṃ brahmatīrthaṃ ca mānada . . 62
1.3.d:
पञ्चतीर्थानि विप्रस्य श्रूयन्ते दक्षिणे करे ।
देवतीर्थं पितृतीर्थं ब्रह्मतीर्थं च मानद ॥ 62
1.3.m: Five holy parts on the right hand of a twice-born are heard of: / the realm of the gods, the realm of the ancestors, and the realm of Brahmā, O giver of honour,

1.3.s:
prājāpatyaṃ tathā cānyattathānyatsaumyamucyate .
aṅguṣṭhamūlottarato yeyaṃ rekhā mahīpate . . 63
1.3.d:
प्राजापत्यं तथा चान्यत्तथान्यत्सौम्यमुच्यते ।
अङ्गुष्ठमूलोत्तरतो येयं रेखा महीपते ॥ 63
1.3.m:
[Another] is called the prājāpatya, and another the saumya.
The line north of the base of the thumb, O king,

1.3.s:
brāhmaṃ tīrthaṃ vadantyetadvasiṣṭhādyā dvijottamāḥ .
kāyaṃ kaniṣṭhikāmūle aṅgulyagre tu daivatam . . 64
1.3.d:
ब्राह्मं तीर्थं वदन्त्येतद्वसिष्ठाद्या द्विजोत्तमाः ।
कायं कनिष्ठिकामूले अङ्गुल्यग्रे तु दैवतम् ॥ 64
1.3.m:
the best of the twice-born, Vasiṣṭha and the others, call the brāhma sacred part.
The kāya is at the root of the little finger, and at the fingertip is the daivata.

1.3.s:
tarjanyaṅguṣṭhayorantaḥ pitryaṃ tīrthamudāhṛtam .
karamadhye sthitaṃ saumyaṃ praśastaṃ devakarmaṇi . . 65
1.3.d:
तर्जन्यङ्गुष्ठयोरन्तः पित्र्यं तीर्थमुदाहृतम् ।
करमध्ये स्थितं सौम्यं प्रशस्तं देवकर्मणि ॥ 65
1.3.m:
Between the forefinger and thumb, the pitrya sacred part is declared.
Situated in the middle of the hand is the saumya, praised in rituals for the gods.

1.3.s:
devārcābaliharaṇaṃ pravikṣapaṇameva ca .
etāni devatīrthena kuryātkurukulodvaha . . 66
1.3.d:
देवार्चाबलिहरणं प्रविक्षपणमेव च ।
एतानि देवतीर्थेन कुर्यात्कुरुकुलोद्वह ॥ 66
1.3.m:
Worship of the gods, offering of bali, and sprinkling [water],
these one should perform with the deva sacred part, O descendant of the Kuru clan.

1.3.s:
annanirvapaṇaṃ rājaṃstathā sapavanaṃ 1 nṛpa .
lājāhomaṃ tathā saumyaṃ prājāpatyena kārayet . . 67
1.3.d:
अन्ननिर्वपणं राजंस्तथा सपवनं 1 नृप ।
लाजाहोमं तथा सौम्यं प्राजापत्येन कारयेत् ॥ 67
1.3.m:
The offering of food, O king, and likewise purification [of grain],
and the parched-grain oblation, O gentle one, one should perform with the prājāpatya.

1.3.s:
kamaṇḍalūpasparśanaṃ dadhiprāśanameva ca .
saumyatīrthena rājendra sadā kuryādvicakṣaṇaḥ . . 68
1.3.d:
कमण्डलूपस्पर्शनं दधिप्राशनमेव च ।
सौम्यतीर्थेन राजेन्द्र सदा कुर्याद्विचक्षणः ॥ 68
1.3.m:
Touching the water pot and consuming curd,
the wise man should always do with the saumya sacred part, O king of kings.

1.3.s:
pitṝṇāṃ tarpaṇaṃ kāryaṃ pitṛtīrthena dhīmatā .
brāhmeṇa cāpi tīrthena sadoṣasparśanaṃ param . . 69
1.3.d:
पितॄणां तर्पणं कार्यं पितृतीर्थेन धीमता ।
ब्राह्मेण चापि तीर्थेन सदोषस्पर्शनं परम् ॥ 69
1.3.m:
The tarpaṇa of the ancestors should be performed with the pitṛ sacred part by the wise man,
and touching with the brāhma sacred part is supreme at all times.

1.3.s:
2ghanāṅgulikaraṃ kṛtvā ekāgraḥ sumanā dvijaḥ .
triḥ kṛtvā yaḥ pibedāpo mukhaśabdavivarjitaḥ . . 1.3.70
1.3.d:
2घनाङ्गुलिकरं कृत्वा एकाग्रः सुमना द्विजः ।
त्रिः कृत्वा यः पिबेदापो मुखशब्दविवर्जितः ॥ 1.3.70
1.3.m:
Joining the fingers tightly of his hand, focused, with a serene mind, a twice-born
who drinks water three times without making a sound with his mouth—

1.3.s:
śṛṇu yatphalamāpnoti prīṇāti ca yathā surān .
prathamaṃ yatpibedāpa ṛgvedastena tṛpyati . . 71
1.3.d:
शृणु यत्फलमाप्नोति प्रीणाति च यथा सुरान् ।
प्रथमं यत्पिबेदाप ऋग्वेदस्तेन तृप्यति ॥ 71
1.3.m:
hear what fruit he obtains and how he pleases the gods:
By the water he drinks first, the Ṛgveda is satisfied;

1.3.s:
yaddvitīyaṃ yajurvedastena prīṇāti bhārata .
yattṛtīyaṃ sāmavedastena prīṇāti bhārata . . 72
1.3.d:
यद्द्वितीयं यजुर्वेदस्तेन प्रीणाति भारत ।
यत्तृतीयं सामवेदस्तेन प्रीणाति भारत ॥ 72
1.3.m:
by the second, the Yajurveda is pleased, O Bhārata;
by the third, the Sāmaveda is pleased, O Bhārata.

1.3.s:
prathamaṃ yanmṛjedāsyaṃ dakṣiṇāṅguṣṭhamūlataḥ .
atharvavedaḥ prīṇāti tena rājannasaṃśayaḥ . . 73
1.3.d:
प्रथमं यन्मृजेदास्यं दक्षिणाङ्गुष्ठमूलतः ।
अथर्ववेदः प्रीणाति तेन राजन्नसंशयः ॥ 73
1.3.m:
When he first wipes his mouth with the base of the right thumb,
the Atharvaveda is pleased thereby, O king, without doubt.

1.3.s:
itihāsapurāṇāni yaddvitīyaṃ pramārjati .
yanmūrdhānaṃ hi rājendra abhiṣiñcati vai dvijaḥ . . 74
1.3.d:
इतिहासपुराणानि यद्द्वितीयं प्रमार्जति ।
यन्मूर्धानं हि राजेन्द्र अभिषिञ्चति वै द्विजः ॥ 74
1.3.m:
When he wipes it a second time, [he pleases] the Itihāsas and Purāṇas.
When the twice-born sprinkles his head, O king of kings,

1.3.s:
tena prīṇāti vai rudraṃ śikhāmālabhya vai ṛṣīn .
yadakṣiṇī cālabhate raviḥ prīṇāti tena vai . . 75
1.3.d:
तेन प्रीणाति वै रुद्रं शिखामालभ्य वै ऋषीन् ।
यदक्षिणी चालभते रविः प्रीणाति तेन वै ॥ 75
1.3.m:
he pleases Rudra thereby; by touching his topknot, [he pleases] the ṛṣis.
When he touches both eyes, the Sun is pleased thereby.

1.3.s:
nāsikālambhanādvāyuṃ prīṇātyeva na saṃśayaḥ .
yacchrotramālabhedvipro diśaḥ prīṇāti tena vai . . 76
1.3.d:
नासिकालम्भनाद्वायुं प्रीणात्येव न संशयः ।
यच्छ्रोत्रमालभेद्विप्रो दिशः प्रीणाति तेन वै ॥ 76
1.3.m:
By touching the nose, he pleases Vāyu, without doubt.
When the twice-born touches the ear, he pleases the directions thereby.

1.3.s:
yamaṃ kuberaṃ varuṇaṃ vāsavaṃ cāgnimeva ca .
yadbāhumanvālabhate etānprīṇāti tena 1 vai . . 77
1.3.d:
यमं कुबेरं वरुणं वासवं चाग्निमेव च ।
यद्बाहुमन्वालभते एतान्प्रीणाति तेन 1 वै ॥ 77
1.3.m:
Yama, Kubera, Varuṇa, Indra, and Agni:
when he touches his arm, he pleases them thereby.

1.3.s:
yannābhimanvālabhate prāṇānāṃ granthimeva ca .
tena prīṇāti rājendra itīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ . . 78
1.3.d:
यन्नाभिमन्वालभते प्राणानां ग्रन्थिमेव च ।
तेन प्रीणाति राजेन्द्र इतीयं वैदिकी श्रुतिः ॥ 78
1.3.m:
When he touches the navel and the knot of the vital breaths,
he pleases [them] thereby, O king of kings; such is the Vedic scripture.

1.3.s:
abhiṣiñcati yatpādau viṣṇuṃ prīṇāti tena vai .
yadbhūmyācchādakaṃ vāri visarjayati mānada . . 79
1.3.d:
अभिषिञ्चति यत्पादौ विष्णुं प्रीणाति तेन वै ।
यद्भूम्याच्छादकं वारि विसर्जयति मानद ॥ 79
1.3.m:
When he sprinkles his feet, he pleases Viṣṇu thereby.
When he releases the water that covers the ground, O giver of honor,

1.3.s:
vāsukipramukhānnāgāṃstena prīṇāti bhārata .
yadbindavo'ntare bhūmau patantīha narādhipa . . 1.3.80
1.3.d:
वासुकिप्रमुखान्नागांस्तेन प्रीणाति भारत ।
यद्बिन्दवोऽन्तरे भूमौ पतन्तीह नराधिप ॥ 1.3.80
1.3.m:
he pleases the serpents headed by Vāsuki, O Bhārata.
When drops fall down here onto the earth, O ruler of men,

1.3.s:
bhūtagrāmaṃ tatastastu prīṇantīha caturvidham .
aṅguṣṭhena pradeśinyā labheta cākṣiṇī nṛpa . . 81
1.3.d:
भूतग्रामं ततस्तस्तु प्रीणन्तीह चतुर्विधम् ।
अङ्गुष्ठेन प्रदेशिन्या लभेत चाक्षिणी नृप ॥ 81
1.3.m:
they please the fourfold host of beings.
One should touch the eyes with the thumb and the forefinger, O king;

1.3.s:
anāmikāṅguṣṭhikābhyāṃ nāsikāmālabhennṛpa .
madhyamāṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ mukhaṃ saṃspṛśedbharatarṣabha . . 82
1.3.d:
अनामिकाङ्गुष्ठिकाभ्यां नासिकामालभेन्नृप ।
मध्यमाङ्गुष्ठाभ्यां मुखं संस्पृशेद्भरतर्षभ ॥ 82
1.3.m:
one should touch the nose with the ring finger and thumb, O king;
one should touch the mouth with the middle finger and thumb, O bull of the Bharatas;

1.3.s:
kaniṣṭhikāṅguṣṭhakābhyāṃ karṇamālabhate nṛpa .
aṅgulībhistathā bāhumaṅguṣṭhena tu maṅgalam . . 83
1.3.d:
कनिष्ठिकाङ्गुष्ठकाभ्यां कर्णमालभते नृप ।
अङ्गुलीभिस्तथा बाहुमङ्गुष्ठेन तु मङ्गलम् ॥ 83
1.3.m:
one touches the ear with the little finger and thumb, O king;
and the arm with the fingers, and what is auspicious with the thumb,

1.3.s:
nābhiṃ kurukulaśreṣṭha śiraḥ sarvābhireva ca .
aṅguṣṭhognirmahābāho prokto vāyuḥ pradeśinī . . 84
1.3.d:
नाभिं कुरुकुलश्रेष्ठ शिरः सर्वाभिरेव च ।
अङ्गुष्ठोग्निर्महाबाहो प्रोक्तो वायुः प्रदेशिनी ॥ 84
1.3.m:
the navel, O best of the Kuru clan, and the head with all [fingers].
The thumb is declared to be Agni, O mighty-armed one; the forefinger is Vāyu;

1.3.s:
anāmikā tathā sūryaḥ kaniṣṭhā māghavā vibho .
prajāpatirmadhyamā jñeyā tasmādbharatasattama . . 85
1.3.d:
अनामिका तथा सूर्यः कनिष्ठा माघवा विभो ।
प्रजापतिर्मध्यमा ज्ञेया तस्माद्भरतसत्तम ॥ 85
1.3.m:
the ring finger is Sūrya; the little finger is Indra, O lord;
the middle finger should be known as Prajāpati; therefore, O best of the Bharatas,

1.3.s:
evamācamya viprastu prīṇāti satataṃ jagat .
sarvāśca devatāstāta lokāṃścāpi na saṃśayaḥ . . 86
1.3.d:
एवमाचम्य विप्रस्तु प्रीणाति सततं जगत् ।
सर्वाश्च देवतास्तात लोकांश्चापि न संशयः ॥ 86
1.3.m:
having sipped water in this way, the twice-born continually pleases the universe,
and all the deities, dear one, and the worlds as well, without doubt.

1.3.s:
tasmātpūjyaḥ sadā vipraḥ sarvadevamayo hi saḥ .
brāhmeṇa vipratīrthena nityakālamupaspṛśet . . 87
1.3.d:
तस्मात्पूज्यः सदा विप्रः सर्वदेवमयो हि सः ।
ब्राह्मेण विप्रतीर्थेन नित्यकालमुपस्पृशेत् ॥ 87
1.3.m:
Therefore, the twice-born is always to be worshipped, for he consists of all the gods.
One should always sip water with the brāhma sacred part of the twice-born,

1.3.s:
kāyatraideśikābhyāṃ vā na pitryeṇa kadācana .
hṛdgābhiḥ pūyate vipraḥ kaṇṭhagābhistu bhūmipaḥ . . 88
1.3.d:
कायत्रैदेशिकाभ्यां वा न पित्र्येण कदाचन ।
हृद्गाभिः पूयते विप्रः कण्ठगाभिस्तु भूमिपः ॥ 88
1.3.m:
or with the kāya and traideśika, never with the pitrya.
A twice-born is purified by [water] reaching the heart, a king by [water] reaching the throat,

1.3.s:
vaiśyodbhiḥ prāśitābhistu śūdraḥ spṛṣṭābhirantataḥ .
uddhṛte dakṣiṇe pāṇāvupavītyucyate budhaḥ . . 89
1.3.d:
वैश्योद्भिः प्राशिताभिस्तु शूद्रः स्पृष्टाभिरन्ततः ।
उद्धृते दक्षिणे पाणावुपवीत्युच्यते बुधः ॥ 89
1.3.m:
a vaiśya by water swallowed, and a śūdra by [water] merely touched.
When the right hand is raised, the wise one is called upavītin;

1.3.s:
savyena prācīnāvītī nivītī kaṇṭhasaṃjñite .
mekhalāmajinaṃ daṇḍamupavītaṃ kamaṇḍalum . . 1.3.90
1.3.d:
सव्येन प्राचीनावीती निवीती कण्ठसंज्ञिते ।
मेखलामजिनं दण्डमुपवीतं कमण्डलुम् ॥ 1.3.90
1.3.m:
with the left, prācīnāvītin; and nivītin when it is around the neck.
The girdle, the black antelope skin, the staff, the sacred thread, and the water pot:

1.3.s:
astu prāsya vinaṣṭāni gṛhṇītānyāni mantravit .
upavītyācamennityamantarjānu mahīpate . . 91
1.3.d:
अस्तु प्रास्य विनष्टानि गृह्णीतान्यानि मन्त्रवित् ।
उपवीत्याचमेन्नित्यमन्तर्जानु महीपते ॥ 91
1.3.m:
having thrown away what is ruined into the water, he who knows the mantras should take others.
Being upavītin, he should always sip water with his hands between his knees, O king.

1.3.s:
evaṃ tu vipro hyācāntaḥ śucitāṃ yāti bhārata .
yāstvetāḥ karamadhye tu rekhā viprasya bhārata . . 92
1.3.d:
एवं तु विप्रो ह्याचान्तः शुचितां याति भारत ।
यास्त्वेताः करमध्ये तु रेखा विप्रस्य भारत ॥ 92
1.3.m:
A twice-born who has sipped water in this way attains purity, O Bhārata.
The lines that are in the middle of the hand of the twice-born, O Bhārata,

1.3.s:
gaṅgādyāḥ saritaḥ sarvā jñeyā bhāratasattama .
yānyaṅguliṣu parvāṇi girayastāni viddhi vai . . 93
1.3.d:
गङ्गाद्याः सरितः सर्वा ज्ञेया भारतसत्तम ।
यान्यङ्गुलिषु पर्वाणि गिरयस्तानि विद्धि वै ॥ 93
1.3.m:
are to be known as all the rivers, beginning with the Gaṅgā, O best of the Bharatas.
Know that the joints in the fingers are the mountains.

1.3.s:
sarvadevamayo rājankaro viprasya dakṣiṇaḥ .
hastopasparśanavidhistavākhyāto mahīpate . . 94
1.3.d:
सर्वदेवमयो राजन्करो विप्रस्य दक्षिणः ।
हस्तोपस्पर्शनविधिस्तवाख्यातो महीपते ॥ 94
1.3.m:
The right hand of the twice-born consists of all the gods, O king.
The rule for touching water with the hand has been told to you, O ruler of the earth,

1.3.s:
eṣu sarveṣu lokeṣu yenācānto divaṃ vrajet . . 95
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ
brāhme parvaṇyupasparśanavidhivarṇanaṃ nāma tṛtīyo'dhyāyaḥ . 3 .
praṇavārthasāvitrīmāhātmyopanayanavidhivarṇanañca
1.3.d:
एषु सर्वेषु लोकेषु येनाचान्तो दिवं व्रजेत् ॥ 95
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां
ब्राह्मे पर्वण्युपस्पर्शनविधिवर्णनं नाम तृतीयोऽध्यायः । 3 ।
प्रणवार्थसावित्रीमाहात्म्योपनयनविधिवर्णनञ्च
1.3.m:
by which, having sipped water, one may go to heaven in all these worlds.
Thus, in the holy Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty thousand verses, in the Brāhmaparvan, the third chapter, named 'Description of the Rule for Sipping Water.' 3.
And the description of the meaning of praṇava, the greatness of the Sāvitrī, and the rule of the upanayana.

1.4.s:
sumanturuvāca
keśāntaḥ ṣoḍaśe varṣe brāhmaṇasya vidhīyate .
rājanyabandhordvāviṃśe vaiśyasya tryadhike tataḥ . . 1
1.4.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
केशान्तः षोडशे वर्षे ब्राह्मणस्य विधीयते ।
राजन्यबन्धोर्द्वाविंशे वैश्यस्य त्र्यधिके ततः ॥ 1
1.4.m:
Sumantu said:
The tonsure of the hair is prescribed in the sixteenth year for a brāhmaṇa,
in the twenty-second for a kṣatriya, and three years after that for a vaiśya.

1.4.s:
amantrikā sadā kāryā strīṇāṃ cūḍā mahīpate .
saṃskārahetoḥ kāyasya yathākālaṃ vibhāgaśaḥ . . 2
1.4.d:
अमन्त्रिका सदा कार्या स्त्रीणां चूडा महीपते ।
संस्कारहेतोः कायस्य यथाकालं विभागशः ॥ 2
1.4.m:
The crest-lock ceremony of women should always be performed without mantras, O king,
for the sake of sanctifying the body, at the proper time, in regular order.

1.4.s:
vaivāhiko vidhiḥ strīṇāṃ saṃskāro naigamaḥ smṛtaḥ .
nivasedvā gurorvāpi gṛhe vāgniparikriyā . . 3
1.4.d:
वैवाहिको विधिः स्त्रीणां संस्कारो नैगमः स्मृतः ।
निवसेद्वा गुरोर्वापि गृहे वाग्निपरिक्रिया ॥ 3
1.4.m:
The marriage rite is traditionally held to be the Vedic saṃskāra for women,
or residing at the house of the guru, or the service of the fire.

1.4.s:
eṣa te kathito rājannaupanāyaniko vidhiḥ .
dvijātīnāṃ mahābāho utpattivyañjakaḥ paraḥ . . 4
1.4.d:
एष ते कथितो राजन्नौपनायनिको विधिः ।
द्विजातीनां महाबाहो उत्पत्तिव्यञ्जकः परः ॥ 4
1.4.m:
This rule of the upanayana has been told to you, O king,
which manifests the supreme birth of the twice-born, O mighty-armed one.

1.4.s:
karmayogamidānīṃ te kathayāmi mahābala .
upanīya guruḥ śiṣyaṃ prathamaṃ śaucamādiśet . . 5
1.4.d:
कर्मयोगमिदानीं ते कथयामि महाबल ।
उपनीय गुरुः शिष्यं प्रथमं शौचमादिशेत् ॥ 5
1.4.m:
Now I shall tell you the yoga of action, O man of great strength.
Having initiated the pupil, the guru should first instruct him in purity,

1.4.s:
ācāramagnikāryaṃ ca sandhyopāsanameva ca .
adhyāpayettu sacchiṣyānsadācānta udaṅmukhaḥ . . 6
1.4.d:
आचारमग्निकार्यं च सन्ध्योपासनमेव च ।
अध्यापयेत्तु सच्छिष्यान्सदाचान्त उदङ्मुखः ॥ 6
1.4.m:
proper conduct, the rites of fire, and the twilight worship.
Having sipped water and facing north, he should teach good pupils.

1.4.s:
brahmāñjalikaro nityamadhyāpyo vijitendriyaḥ .
laghuvāsāstathaikāgraḥ sumanā supratiṣṭhitaḥ . . 7
1.4.d:
ब्रह्माञ्जलिकरो नित्यमध्याप्यो विजितेन्द्रियः ।
लघुवासास्तथैकाग्रः सुमना सुप्रतिष्ठितः ॥ 7
1.4.m:
With hands joined in reverence for sacred study, he should always be taught, his senses conquered,
wearing light garments, focused, with a serene mind, and well-seated.

1.4.s:
brahmārambhe'vasāne ca pādau pūjyau guroḥ sadā .
saṃhatya hastāvadhyeyaṃ sa hi brahmāñjaliḥ smṛtaḥ . . 8
1.4.d:
ब्रह्मारम्भेऽवसाने च पादौ पूज्यौ गुरोः सदा ।
संहत्य हस्तावध्येयं स हि ब्रह्माञ्जलिः स्मृतः ॥ 8
1.4.m:
At the beginning and at the end of sacred study, the feet of the guru should always be revered.
Study should be done with joined hands; for that is remembered as the brahmāñjali.

1.4.s:
vyatyastapāṇinā kāryamupasaṅgrahaṇaṃ guroḥ .
savyena savyaḥ spraṣṭavyo dakṣiṇena tu dakṣiṇaḥ . . 9
1.4.d:
व्यत्यस्तपाणिना कार्यमुपसङ्ग्रहणं गुरोः ।
सव्येन सव्यः स्प्रष्टव्यो दक्षिणेन तु दक्षिणः ॥ 9
1.4.m:
The clasping of the guru's feet should be done with crossed hands;
the left [foot] is to be touched with the left, and the right with the right.

1.4.s:
adhyeṣyamāṇaṃ tu gururnityakālamatandritaḥ .
adhīṣva bho iti brūyādvirāmo'stviti vārayet . . 1.4.10
1.4.d:
अध्येष्यमाणं तु गुरुर्नित्यकालमतन्द्रितः ।
अधीष्व भो इति ब्रूयाद्विरामोऽस्त्विति वारयेत् ॥ 1.4.10
1.4.m:
To him who is about to study, the guru, always unwearied,
should say, 'Sir, study!' and should dismiss him saying, 'Let there be a pause.'

1.4.s:
brahmaṇaḥ praṇavaṃ kuryādādāvante ca sarvadā .
sravatyanoṅkṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ parastācca viśīryate . . 11
1.4.d:
ब्रह्मणः प्रणवं कुर्यादादावन्ते च सर्वदा ।
स्रवत्यनोङ्कृतं पूर्वं परस्ताच्च विशीर्यते ॥ 11
1.4.m:
One should always utter the praṇava at the beginning and at the end of the Veda;
not preceded by Oṃ, it leaks away, and [without it] at the end, it disintegrates.

1.4.s:
śrūyatāṃ cāpi rājendra yathoṅkāraṃ dvijo'rhati .
prākkūlānparyupāsīnaḥ pavitraiścaiva pāvitaḥ . . 12
1.4.d:
श्रूयतां चापि राजेन्द्र यथोङ्कारं द्विजोऽर्हति ।
प्राक्कूलान्पर्युपासीनः पवित्रैश्चैव पावितः ॥ 12
1.4.m:
Hear also, O king of kings, how the twice-born is entitled to the syllable Oṃ:
sitting near [kusa grass] with tips pointed eastward and purified by purifying strainers,

1.4.s:
prāṇāyāmaistribhiḥ pūtastatastvoṅkāramarhati .
oṃkāralakṣaṇaṃ cāpi śṛṇuṣva kurunandana . . 13
1.4.d:
प्राणायामैस्त्रिभिः पूतस्ततस्त्वोङ्कारमर्हति ।
ओंकारलक्षणं चापि शृणुष्व कुरुनन्दन ॥ 13
1.4.m: Purified by three breath-controls, he then deserves the syllable Oṃ. / Hear also the characteristic mark of the syllable Oṃ, O son of Kuru:

1.4.s:
akāraṃ cāpyukāraṃ ca makāraṃ ca prajāpatiḥ .
vedatrayāttu nirgṛhya bhūrbhuvaḥ svaritīti ca . . 14
1.4.d:
अकारं चाप्युकारं च मकारं च प्रजापतिः ।
वेदत्रयात्तु निर्गृह्य भूर्भुवः स्वरितीति च ॥ 14
1.4.m: Prajāpati extracted the sound 'a', the sound 'u', / and the sound 'ma' from the three Vedas, as well as [the utterances] 'bhūḥ', 'bhuvaḥ', and 'svaḥ'.

1.4.s:
tribhya eva tu vedebhyaḥ pādaṃpādamadūduhat .
tadityṛco'syāḥ sāvitryāḥ parameṣṭhī prajāpatiḥ . . 15
1.4.d:
त्रिभ्य एव तु वेदेभ्यः पादंपादमदूदुहत् ।
तदित्यृचोऽस्याः सावित्र्याः परमेष्ठी प्रजापतिः ॥ 15
1.4.m: From the three Vedas alone the supreme lord Prajāpati milked / verse-quarter by verse-quarter that Sāvitrī verse, 'tat [savitur vareṇyam...]'.

1.4.s:
etadakṣarametāṃ ca japanvyāhṛtipūrvikām .
sandhyayorubhayorvipro veda puṇyena yujyate . . 16
1.4.d:
एतदक्षरमेतां च जपन्व्याहृतिपूर्विकाम् ।
सन्ध्ययोरुभयोर्विप्रो वेद पुण्येन युज्यते ॥ 16
1.4.m: Repeating this syllable and this [verse] preceded by the utterances / at both twilight junctions, a brāhmaṇa is united with the merit of the Veda.

1.4.s:
sahasrakṛtvastvabhyasya bahiretattrikaṃ dvijaḥ .
mahato'pyenaso māsāttvacevāhirvimucyate . . 17
1.4.d:
सहस्रकृत्वस्त्वभ्यस्य बहिरेतत्त्रिकं द्विजः ।
महतोऽप्येनसो मासात्त्वचेवाहिर्विमुच्यते ॥ 17
1.4.m: Having recited this triad outside [the village] a thousand times, / a twice-born is freed even from great sin within a month, as a snake from its slough.

1.4.s:
etayarcā visaṃyuktaḥ kāle ca kriyayā svayā .
viprakṣatriyaviḍyonirgarhaṇāṃ yāti sādhuṣu . . 18
1.4.d:
एतयर्चा विसंयुक्तः काले च क्रियया स्वया ।
विप्रक्षत्रियविड्योनिर्गर्हणां याति साधुषु ॥ 18
1.4.m: Deprived of this verse and of his proper rite at its due time, / one born of brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, or vaiśya origin incurs censure among the virtuous.

1.4.s:
śṛṇuṣvaikamanā rājanparamaṃ brahmaṇo mukham .
oṃkārapūrvikāstisro mahāvyāhṛtayo'vyayāḥ . . 19
1.4.d:
शृणुष्वैकमना राजन्परमं ब्रह्मणो मुखम् ।
ओंकारपूर्विकास्तिस्रो महाव्याहृतयोऽव्ययाः ॥ 19
1.4.m: Listen with single-minded focus, O king, to the supreme mouth of the Veda: / the three imperishable great utterances preceded by the syllable Oṃ,

1.4.s:
tripadā caiva sāvitrī vijñeyā brahmaṇo mukham .
yo'dhīte'hanyahanyetāṃ trīṇi varṣāṇyatandritaḥ . . 1.4.20
1.4.d:
त्रिपदा चैव सावित्री विज्ञेया ब्रह्मणो मुखम् ।
योऽधीतेऽहन्यहन्येतां त्रीणि वर्षाण्यतन्द्रितः ॥ 1.4.20
1.4.m: and the three-footed Sāvitrī are to be known as the mouth of the Veda. / He who studies this daily for three years without slackening

1.4.s:
sa brahma paramabhyeti vāyubhūtaḥ khamūrtimān .
ekākṣaraṃ paraṃ brahma prāṇāyāmaḥ parantapa . . 21
1.4.d:
स ब्रह्म परमभ्येति वायुभूतः खमूर्तिमान् ।
एकाक्षरं परं ब्रह्म प्राणायामः परन्तप ॥ 21
1.4.m: attains the supreme Brahman, becoming wind and having the form of ether. / The single syllable is the supreme Brahman; breath-control is [the supreme] austerity, O scorcher of foes.

1.4.s:
sāvitryāstu paraṃ nāsti maunātsatyaṃ viśiṣyate .
tapaḥ kiyā homakriyā tathā dānakriyā nṛpa . . 22
1.4.d:
सावित्र्यास्तु परं नास्ति मौनात्सत्यं विशिष्यते ।
तपः किया होमक्रिया तथा दानक्रिया नृप ॥ 22
1.4.m: There is nothing higher than the Sāvitrī; truth is superior to silence. / Austerity, oblation-rites, and charitable gifts, O king,

1.4.s:
akṣayāntāḥ sadā rājanyathāha bhagavānmanuḥ .
avaraṃ svakṣaraṃ jñeyaṃ brahma caiva prajāpatiḥ . . 23
1.4.d:
अक्षयान्ताः सदा राजन्यथाह भगवान्मनुः ।
अवरं स्वक्षरं ज्ञेयं ब्रह्म चैव प्रजापतिः ॥ 23
1.4.m: have a finite end, O king, as the blessed Manu has declared; / but the imperishable syllable is to be known as the highest, and Brahman is Prajāpati himself.

1.4.s:
vidhiyajñātsadā rājañjapayajño viśiṣyate .
nānāvidhairguṇoddeśaiḥ sūkṣmākhyātairnṛpottama . . 24
1.4.d:
विधियज्ञात्सदा राजञ्जपयज्ञो विशिष्यते ।
नानाविधैर्गुणोद्देशैः सूक्ष्माख्यातैर्नृपोत्तम ॥ 24
1.4.m: The sacrifice of recitation is always superior to the ritual sacrifice, O king, / through various enumerated virtues that are explained in subtle detail, O best of kings.

1.4.s:
pāṃśuḥ syāllakṣaguṇaḥ sahasro mānasaḥ smṛtaḥ .
ye pākayajñāścatvāro vidhiyajñena cānvitāḥ . . 25
1.4.d:
पांशुः स्याल्लक्षगुणः सहस्रो मानसः स्मृतः ।
ये पाकयज्ञाश्चत्वारो विधियज्ञेन चान्विताः ॥ 25
1.4.m: The whispered [prayer] is said to be a hundred thousand times [greater], and the mental one a thousand [times greater than that]. / The four domestic sacrifices, together with the ritual sacrifice,

1.4.s:
sarve te japayajñasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm .
japādeva tu saṃsidhyeddbrāhmaṇo nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 26
1.4.d:
सर्वे ते जपयज्ञस्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम् ।
जपादेव तु संसिध्येद्द्ब्राह्मणो नात्र संशयः ॥ 26
1.4.m: do not all equal a sixteenth part of the sacrifice of recitation. / By recitation alone a brāhmaṇa attains perfection; of this there is no doubt.

1.4.s:
kuryādanyanna vā kuryānmaitro brāhmaṇa ucyate .
pūrvāṃ sandhyāṃ japaṃstiṣṭhetsāvitrīmārkadarśanāt . . 27
1.4.d:
कुर्यादन्यन्न वा कुर्यान्मैत्रो ब्राह्मण उच्यते ।
पूर्वां सन्ध्यां जपंस्तिष्ठेत्सावित्रीमार्कदर्शनात् ॥ 27
1.4.m: Whether he performs other rites or not, a brāhmaṇa is called a friend [to all]. / Reciting the Sāvitrī, he should stand during the morning twilight until the appearance of the sun,

1.4.s:
paścimāṃ tu samāsīnaḥ samyagṛkṣavibhāvanāt .
dinasyādau bhavetpūrvā śarvaryādau tathā parā . . 28
1.4.d:
पश्चिमां तु समासीनः सम्यगृक्षविभावनात् ।
दिनस्यादौ भवेत्पूर्वा शर्वर्यादौ तथा परा ॥ 28
1.4.m: and seated during the evening [twilight] until the stars appear clearly. / The morning [twilight] is at the start of day, and the other is at the start of night.

1.4.s:
sanakṣatrā parā jñeyā aparā sadivākarā .
japaṃstiṣṭhanparāṃ sandhyāṃ naiśameno vyapohati . . 29
1.4.d:
सनक्षत्रा परा ज्ञेया अपरा सदिवाकरा ।
जपंस्तिष्ठन्परां सन्ध्यां नैशमेनो व्यपोहति ॥ 29
1.4.m: The evening one is to be known as attended by stars, the other [morning one] attended by the sun. / Standing and reciting at the evening twilight, he dispels the sin committed by night;

1.4.s:
aparāṃ tu samāsīno malaṃ hanti divākṛtam .
nopatiṣṭhati yaḥ pūrvāṃ nopāste paścimāṃ nṛpa . . 1.4.30
1.4.d:
अपरां तु समासीनो मलं हन्ति दिवाकृतम् ।
नोपतिष्ठति यः पूर्वां नोपास्ते पश्चिमां नृप ॥ 1.4.30
1.4.m: and seated during the other [morning twilight], he destroys the blemish caused by day. / He who does not stand for the morning [twilight] nor attend the evening [twilight], O king,

1.4.s:
sa śūdravadbahiṣkāryaḥ sarvasmāddvijakarmaṇaḥ .
apāṃ samīpe niyato naityakaṃ vidhimāsthitaḥ . . 31
1.4.d:
स शूद्रवद्बहिष्कार्यः सर्वस्माद्द्विजकर्मणः ।
अपां समीपे नियतो नैत्यकं विधिमास्थितः ॥ 31
1.4.m: should be excluded, like a śūdra, from all rites of the twice-born. / Restrained near water, adhering to the daily obligatory rite,

1.4.s:
sāvitrīmapyadhīyīta gatyā'raṇyaṃ samāhitaḥ .
vedopakaraṇe rājansvādhyāye caiva naityake . . 32
1.4.d:
सावित्रीमप्यधीयीत गत्याऽरण्यं समाहितः ।
वेदोपकरणे राजन्स्वाध्याये चैव नैत्यके ॥ 32
1.4.m: he should also recite the Sāvitrī, having gone to the forest with collected mind. / In the auxiliary Vedic texts, O king, and in daily Vedic recitation,

1.4.s:
nātra doṣostyanadhyāye homamantreṣu vā vibho .
naityake nāstvanadhyāyo brahmasatraṃ hi tatkṛtam . . 33
1.4.d:
नात्र दोषोस्त्यनध्याये होममन्त्रेषु वा विभो ।
नैत्यके नास्त्वनध्यायो ब्रह्मसत्रं हि तत्कृतम् ॥ 33
1.4.m: there is no fault of non-recitation days, nor in the mantras of oblations, O lord. / For the daily obligatory [study] there is no non-recitation day, for that is performed as a Brahma-sacrifice.

1.4.s:
brahmāhutihutaṃ puṣyamanadhyāyavaṣaṭkṛtam .
ṛgekāṃ yastvadhīyīta vidhinā niyato dvijaḥ . . 34
1.4.d:
ब्रह्माहुतिहुतं पुष्यमनध्यायवषट्कृतम् ।
ऋगेकां यस्त्वधीयीत विधिना नियतो द्विजः ॥ 34
1.4.m: The offering made as an oblation to Brahman flourishes, consecrated as vaṣaṭ even on non-recitation days. / A twice-born who, being self-controlled, studies even a single Ṛg verse according to rule,

1.4.s:
tasya nityaṃ kṣaratyeṣā payo medhyaṃ ghṛtaṃ madhu .
agniśuśrūṣaṇaṃ bhaikṣamadhaḥ śayyāṃ gurorhitam . . 35
1.4.d:
तस्य नित्यं क्षरत्येषा पयो मेध्यं घृतं मधु ।
अग्निशुश्रूषणं भैक्षमधः शय्यां गुरोर्हितम् ॥ 35
1.4.m: for him it continually flows with milk, pure ghee, and honey. / Tending the sacred fire, begging for alms, sleeping on the ground, doing what is beneficial for the guru,

1.4.s:
āsamāvartanātkuryātkṛtopanayano dvijaḥ .
ācāryaputraśuśrūṣāṃ jñānado dhārmikaḥ śuciḥ . . 36
1.4.d:
आसमावर्तनात्कुर्यात्कृतोपनयनो द्विजः ।
आचार्यपुत्रशुश्रूषां ज्ञानदो धार्मिकः शुचिः ॥ 36
1.4.m: a twice-born who has undergone initiation should perform these until his return home. / Service to the teacher's son, one who imparts knowledge, the virtuous, the pure,

1.4.s:
āptaḥ śaktonnadaḥ sādhuḥ svādhyāpyā daśa dharmataḥ .
nāpṛṣṭaḥ kasyacidbrūyānna cānyāyena pṛcchataḥ . . 37
1.4.d:
आप्तः शक्तोन्नदः साधुः स्वाध्याप्या दश धर्मतः ।
नापृष्टः कस्यचिद्ब्रूयान्न चान्यायेन पृच्छतः ॥ 37
1.4.m: the trustworthy, the capable, the provider of food, and the good: these ten may be taught according to dharma. / One should not speak to anyone unasked, nor to someone who asks improperly.

1.4.s:
jānannapi hi medhāvī jaḍavalloka ācaret .
adharmeṇa ca yaḥ prāha yaścādharmeṇa pṛcchati . . 38
1.4.d:
जानन्नपि हि मेधावी जडवल्लोक आचरेत् ।
अधर्मेण च यः प्राह यश्चाधर्मेण पृच्छति ॥ 38
1.4.m: Even though he knows, an intelligent person should act in the world as if he were mute. / Both he who speaks contrary to dharma and he who asks contrary to dharma—

1.4.s:
tayoranyataraḥ praiti vidveṣaṃ vā nigacchati .
dharmārthau yatra na syātāṃ śuśrūṣā cāpi tadvidhā . .
na tatra vidyā vaptavyā śubhaṃ bījamivoṣare . . 39
1.4.d:
तयोरन्यतरः प्रैति विद्वेषं वा निगच्छति ।
धर्मार्थौ यत्र न स्यातां शुश्रूषा चापि तद्विधा ॥
न तत्र विद्या वप्तव्या शुभं बीजमिवोषरे ॥ 39
1.4.m: one of the two dies, or incurs enmity. / Where dharma and material gain are not present, nor obedient service of that kind, / learning should not be sown there, like good seed in barren soil.

1.4.s:
vidyayaiva samaṃ kāmaṃ martavyaṃ brahmavādinā .
āpadyapi hi ghorāyāṃ na tvenāmīriṇe vapet . .1.4.4 0
vidyā brāhmaṇamityāha śevadhiste'smi rakṣa mām .
asūyakāya mā prādāstathā syāṃ vīryavattamā . .4 1
śevaṃ sukhamuśantīha kecijjñānaṃ pracakṣate .
tau dhārayati vai yasmācchevadhistena socyate . .42
1.4.d:
विद्ययैव समं कामं मर्तव्यं ब्रह्मवादिना ।
आपद्यपि हि घोरायां न त्वेनामीरिणे वपेत् ॥1.4.4 0
विद्या ब्राह्मणमित्याह शेवधिस्तेऽस्मि रक्ष माम् ।
असूयकाय मा प्रादास्तथा स्यां वीर्यवत्तमा ॥4 1
शेवं सुखमुशन्तीह केचिज्ज्ञानं प्रचक्षते ।
तौ धारयति वै यस्माच्छेवधिस्तेन सोच्यते ॥42
1.4.m: A teacher of the Veda should rather die along with his learning; / even in dire distress he must not sow it in barren ground. / Learning said to a brāhmaṇa: 'I am your treasure, protect me; / do not bestow me on an envious person, so that I may remain exceedingly potent.' / 'Śeva' they explain here as happiness, while some declare it to be knowledge; / because it holds both of those, it is therefore called a treasure [śevadhi].

1.4.s:
yameva tu śuciṃ vidyānniyataṃ brahmacāriṇam .
tasmai māṃ brūhi viprāya nidhipāyāpramādine . .4 3
brahma yastvananujñātamadhīyānādavāpnuyāt . . 44
1.4.d:
यमेव तु शुचिं विद्यान्नियतं ब्रह्मचारिणम् ।
तस्मै मां ब्रूहि विप्राय निधिपायाप्रमादिने ॥4 3
ब्रह्म यस्त्वननुज्ञातमधीयानादवाप्नुयात् ॥ 44
1.4.m: 'Deliver me only to that brāhmaṇa whom you know to be pure, / self-controlled, celibate, heedful, and a guardian of the treasure.' / But he who obtains sacred lore from someone studying without permission,

1.4.s:
laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ vāpi tathādhyātmikameva ca .
sa yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ rauravaṃ bhīmadarśanam . . 45
1.4.d:
लौकिकं वैदिकं वापि तथाध्यात्मिकमेव च ।
स याति नरकं घोरं रौरवं भीमदर्शनम् ॥ 45
1.4.m: whether secular, Vedic, or spiritual, / goes to the dreadful Raurava hell, terrible to behold.

1.4.s:
aṇumātrātmakaṃ dehaṃ ṣoḍaśārdhamiti smṛtam .
ādadīta yato jñānaṃ taṃ pūrvamabhivādayet . . 46
1.4.d:
अणुमात्रात्मकं देहं षोडशार्धमिति स्मृतम् ।
आददीत यतो ज्ञानं तं पूर्वमभिवादयेत् ॥ 46
1.4.m: A body consisting merely of subtle parts is traditionally remembered as eightfold. / He from whom one receives knowledge, him one should salute with reverence first.

1.4.s:
sāvitrīsāramātro'pi varo vipraḥ suyantritaḥ .
nāyantritastrivedo'pi sarvāśī sarvavikrayī . . 47
1.4.d:
सावित्रीसारमात्रोऽपि वरो विप्रः सुयन्त्रितः ।
नायन्त्रितस्त्रिवेदोऽपि सर्वाशी सर्वविक्रयी ॥ 47
1.4.m: A brāhmaṇa who merely masters the Sāvitrī, if well-restrained, is superior; / not one who knows the three Vedas but is unrestrained, eating everything and selling everything.

1.4.s:
śayyāsanedhyācarite śreyasā na samāviśet .
śayyāsanasthaścaivenaṃ pratyutthāyābhivādayet . . 48
1.4.d:
शय्यासनेध्याचरिते श्रेयसा न समाविशेत् ।
शय्यासनस्थश्चैवेनं प्रत्युत्थायाभिवादयेत् ॥ 48
1.4.m: One should not occupy a bed or seat that is used by a superior; / and seated upon a bed or seat, one should rise to greet him with reverence.

1.4.s:
ūrdhvaṃ prāṇā hyutkrāmanti yūnaḥ sthavira āgate .
pratyutthānābhivādābhyāṃ punastānpratipadyate . . 49
1.4.d:
ऊर्ध्वं प्राणा ह्युत्क्रामन्ति यूनः स्थविर आगते ।
प्रत्युत्थानाभिवादाभ्यां पुनस्तान्प्रतिपद्यते ॥ 49
1.4.m: For the vital breaths of a young man ascend upwards when an elder arrives; / by rising up and saluting with reverence, he recovers them again.

1.4.s:
abhivādanaśīlasya nityaṃ vṛddhopasevinaḥ .
catvāri samyagvardhante āyuḥ prajñā yaśo balam . . 1.4.50
1.4.d:
अभिवादनशीलस्य नित्यं वृद्धोपसेविनः ।
चत्वारि सम्यग्वर्धन्ते आयुः प्रज्ञा यशो बलम् ॥ 1.4.50
1.4.m: For one who is accustomed to respectful salutation and who continually attends upon elders, / four things increase properly: life span, wisdom, fame, and strength.

1.4.s:
abhivādaparo vipro jyāyāṃsamabhivādayet .
asau nāmāhamasmīti svanāma parikīrtayet . . 51
1.4.d:
अभिवादपरो विप्रो ज्यायांसमभिवादयेत् ।
असौ नामाहमस्मीति स्वनाम परिकीर्तयेत् ॥ 51
1.4.m: A brāhmaṇa devoted to respectful salutation should salute an elder; / he should announce his own name, saying, 'I am such-and-such by name.'

1.4.s:
nāmadheyasya ye kecidabhivādaṃ na jānate .
tānprājño'hamiti brūyātstriyaḥ sarvāstathaiva ca . . 52
1.4.d:
नामधेयस्य ये केचिदभिवादं न जानते ।
तान्प्राज्ञोऽहमिति ब्रूयात्स्त्रियः सर्वास्तथैव च ॥ 52
1.4.m: To those who do not understand the salutation by name, / a wise man should say, 'It is I', and likewise to all women.

1.4.s:
bhoḥ śabdaṃ kīrtayedante svasya nāmnobhivādane .
nāmnaḥ svarūpabhāvo hi bho bhāva ṛṣibhiḥ smṛtaḥ . . 53
1.4.d:
भोः शब्दं कीर्तयेदन्ते स्वस्य नाम्नोभिवादने ।
नाम्नः स्वरूपभावो हि भो भाव ऋषिभिः स्मृतः ॥ 53
1.4.m: He should pronounce the word 'bhoḥ' at the end of his own name in salutation; / for the inherent nature of a name is remembered by the sages as the state of 'bhoḥ'.

1.4.s:
āyuṣmānbhava saumyeti vācyo vipro'bhivādane .
akāraścāsya nāmno'nte vācyaḥ pūrvākṣaraḥ plutaḥ . . 54
1.4.d:
आयुष्मान्भव सौम्येति वाच्यो विप्रोऽभिवादने ।
अकारश्चास्य नाम्नोऽन्ते वाच्यः पूर्वाक्षरः प्लुतः ॥ 54
1.4.m: A brāhmaṇa should be addressed in return of a salutation with: 'May you be long-lived, gentle one'; / and at the end of his name, the vowel 'a' should be spoken with the preceding syllable prolated.

1.4.s:
yo na vettyabhivādasya vipraḥ pratyabhivādanam .
nābhivādyaḥ sa viduṣā yathā śūdrastathaiva saḥ . . 55
1.4.d:
यो न वेत्त्यभिवादस्य विप्रः प्रत्यभिवादनम् ।
नाभिवाद्यः स विदुषा यथा शूद्रस्तथैव सः ॥ 55
1.4.m: A brāhmaṇa who does not know how to return a salutation / should not be saluted by a learned man; he is just like a śūdra.

1.4.s:
abhivāde kṛte yastu na karotyabhivādanam .
āśīrvā kuruśārdūla sa yāti narakaṃ dhruvam . . 56
1.4.d:
अभिवादे कृते यस्तु न करोत्यभिवादनम् ।
आशीर्वा कुरुशार्दूल स याति नरकं ध्रुवम् ॥ 56
1.4.m: He who, when a salutation has been made, does not return a salutation / or a blessing, O tiger of the Kurus, goes surely to hell.

1.4.s:
abhīti bhagavānviṣṇuārvādayāmīti śaṅkaraḥ .
dvāveva pūjitau tena yaḥ karotyabhivādanam . . 57
1.4.d:
अभीति भगवान्विष्णुआर्वादयामीति शङ्करः ।
द्वावेव पूजितौ तेन यः करोत्यभिवादनम् ॥ 57
1.4.m: 'Abhi' is the blessed Viṣṇu, and 'I salute' [vādāyami] is Śaṅkara; / both of them are worshipped by him who performs a salutation.

1.4.s:
brāhmaṇaṃ kuśalaṃ pṛcchetkṣatrabandhumanāmayam .
vaiśyaṃ kṣemaṃ samāgamya śūdramārogyameva tu . . 58
1.4.d:
ब्राह्मणं कुशलं पृच्छेत्क्षत्रबन्धुमनामयम् ।
वैश्यं क्षेमं समागम्य शूद्रमारोग्यमेव तु ॥ 58
1.4.m: One should ask a brāhmaṇa about his well-being, an associate of the kṣatriya class about freedom from illness, / a vaiśya, upon meeting, about prosperity, and a śūdra about good health.

1.4.s:
na vācyo dīkṣito nāmnā yavīyānapi yo bhavet .
bho bhavatpūrvakatvena iti svāyambhuvo'bravīt . 59
1.4.d:
न वाच्यो दीक्षितो नाम्ना यवीयानपि यो भवेत् ।
भो भवत्पूर्वकत्वेन इति स्वायम्भुवोऽब्रवीत् । 59
1.4.m: An initiated person, even if younger, should not be addressed by name, / but rather preceded by "bho" or "bhavat"—so spoke the Self-born Manu.

1.4.s:
parapatnī tu yā rājannasambaddhā tu yonitaḥ .
vaktavyā bhavatītyevaṃ subhage bhaganīti ca . . 1.4.60
1.4.d:
परपत्नी तु या राजन्नसम्बद्धा तु योनितः ।
वक्तव्या भवतीत्येवं सुभगे भगनीति च ॥ 1.4.60
1.4.m: Another’s wife, O king, who is not related by blood, / should be addressed as "bhavatī", "fortunate one", or "sister".

1.4.s:
pitṛvyānmātulānrājañchvaśurānṛtvijo gurūn .
asāvahamiti brūyātpratyutthāya jaghanyajaḥ . . 61
1.4.d:
पितृव्यान्मातुलान्राजञ्छ्वशुरानृत्विजो गुरून् ।
असावहमिति ब्रूयात्प्रत्युत्थाय जघन्यजः ॥ 61
1.4.m: To paternal uncles, maternal uncles, O king, fathers-in-law, priests, and elders, / a younger person should rise and say, "I am so-and-so".

1.4.s:
mātṛṣvasā mātulānī śvaśrūratha pitṛṣvasā .
sampūjyā gurupatnī ca samāstā gurubhāryayā . . 62
1.4.d:
